GHOSTWIRE.ModuleDescription: Ghostwire content and presentation for Draw Steel on Foundry VTT.

Characteristics.MapHint: Ghostwire display labels map onto Draw Steel characteristics: Physique=Might, Reflex=Agility, Logic=Reason, Instinct=Intuition, Persona=Presence.

Abilities.NotEnoughResource: {name} costs {cost} {resource}, and you have {current}. You can’t use it in combat until you have enough.

Rush.Name: Rush
Rush.Description:
When a creature takes the Rush main action, they move up to their speed in a straight line without jumping, then make a @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel.abilities.Item.wU69Y06G9lYFrvp6]{melee free strike} against a target when they end their move. If the creature has an ability with the Rush keyword, they can use that ability against the target instead of a free strike.

A creature can’t move through difficult terrain or shift when they rush. They can fly or burrow as part of the Rush main action if they have that movement available to them — thrusters, grav rigs, and tunneling gear included — but they can’t climb or swim while rushing unless they can automatically use that movement at full speed.

TakeCover.Name: Take Cover
TakeCover.Description: When a creature takes the [[/apply TYggdI2Kwa302NjW]]{Take Cover main action}, they get low behind whatever the street offers — an engine block, a dumpster, a doorframe — and ability rolls made against them have a double bane until the start of their next turn. Additionally, you have a double edge on tests when called for to resist environmental effects or a creature’s traits or abilities. A creature gains no benefit from this action while another creature is taunted by them.
TakeCover.EffectDescription: Ability rolls made against you have a double bane until the start of your next turn. You have a double edge on tests when called for to resist environmental effects or a creature’s traits or abilities. You gain no benefit from this while another creature is taunted by you.

PatchUp.Name: Patch Up
PatchUp.Description: A creature who uses the Patch Up main action slaps on a trauma patch, jabs a stim, or talks an adjacent creature through the pain to keep them in the fight. The target creature can spend a Recovery to regain Stamina, or can make a saving throw against one effect they are suffering that is ended by a saving throw.

SpotTarget.Name: Spot Target
SpotTarget.Description: Choose an enemy adjacent to you and tag it for your crew — a callout, a laser dot, a ping on the shared feed. The next ability power roll an ally makes against that creature before the start of your next turn has an edge.

Drive.Name: Drive
Drive.Description: A creature can take the Drive move action only while piloting a vehicle. When a creature takes the Drive move action, they cause their vehicle to move up to the vehicle’s speed, taking the driver and any passengers with it. Alternatively, a creature can use the Drive move action to have their vehicle use the Disengage move action as a free triggered action. A creature can use the Drive move action only once per round. A vehicle can only have this move action applied to it once per round. This movement can be broken up with the driver’s maneuver and main action however they wish.

Connect.Name: Connect
Connect.Story: You plug your Persona into the Wired where you stand.
Connect.Effect:
You establish a Persona in the Wired at your current location and enter the Overlay connection state. Until you Connect, you can’t use the other Matrix Verbs, Programs, or Wired abilities that require you to be Overlaid or Jacked In.

Hacking: if you have the Hacking skill, this verb’s power roll gains an edge. Jacked In: the roll also gains an edge.

JackOut.Name: Jack Out
JackOut.Story: Eject. Your full attention slams back into your body.
JackOut.Effect:
You disconnect from the Wired, leaving Overlay or Jacked In, and return your full attention to the physical world. This is your emergency eject when biofeedback spikes or hostile ICE locks on.

Emergency: in a genuine emergency, you can use Jack Out as a free triggered action instead of a maneuver.

Hacking: if you have the Hacking skill, this verb’s power roll gains an edge. Jacked In: the roll also gains an edge.

ToggleConnectionState.Name: Toggle Connection State
ToggleConnectionState.Story: Half in, or all the way under. Your call, always.
ToggleConnectionState.Effect:
While you are connected to the Wired, you switch between Overlay and Jacked In without disconnecting. No roll and no contest.

  • Overlay: the Wired rides over your physical senses. You can still see, move, speak, and act physically, but your real-world power rolls take a bane.

  • Jacked In: full immersion. Your Wired power rolls gain an edge, but your body is inert: you can’t perceive, move, or act in the physical world, and you can’t make real-world power rolls.

You can’t use this ability while disconnected.

Scan.Name: Scan
Scan.Story: What’s here? Doors, cameras, locks, drones — everything with a signal.
Scan.Effect:
You get a read on the nodes within your Reach: doors, cameras, locks, drones, and any other Wired-connected system in range. Passive observation doesn’t raise the Trace Alert on its own.

Hacking: if you have the Hacking skill, this verb’s power roll gains an edge. Jacked In: the roll also gains an edge.

Navigate.Name: Navigate
Navigate.Story: Movement, Wired-side: you slide node to node.
Navigate.Effect:
You move through the Wired up to your Reach in nodes, repositioning your Persona to reach a node, ally, or target you couldn’t otherwise touch.

Hacking: if you have the Hacking skill, this verb’s power roll gains an edge. Jacked In: the roll also gains an edge.

Ping.Name: Ping
Ping.Story: A light tap on a simple system — flick a light, test a lock.
Ping.Effect:
You give a simple, low-stakes nudge to one simple Track 1 object within your Reach — flick a light, tap a lock, test a system — without needing a cyberdeck or a full Program.

Hacking: if you have the Hacking skill, this verb’s power roll gains an edge. Jacked In: the roll also gains an edge.

Broadcast.Name: Broadcast
Broadcast.Story: A private channel nobody outside the link can hear.
Broadcast.Effect: You send a message to allies you’re already connected to, within your Reach or Ghost Distance, over a private Wired-only channel no one outside the link can intercept. No roll and no contest; it just works.

Search.Name: Search
Search.Story: Scan tells you what’s around. Search tells you what’s buried.
Search.Effect:
You dig into a node you’re already at to find something specific hiding inside it — the follow-up to Scan.

Hacking: if you have the Hacking skill, this verb’s power roll gains an edge. Jacked In: the roll also gains an edge.

ReadWrite.Name: Read/Write
ReadWrite.Story: Read the file. Change the record. Plant the evidence. Forge the badge.
ReadWrite.Effect:
You read a file’s contents, alter a record, plant or delete evidence, or forge a credential in a node you’re at. This is the verb that actually changes information in the Wired.

Hacking: if you have the Hacking skill, this verb’s power roll gains an edge. Jacked In: the roll also gains an edge.

StreetEye.Name: Street Eye
StreetEye.Story: A soft leash on one scout in the air — follow, watch, hold, or mark a corner.
StreetEye.Description:
Street Eye (rules name: Companion Link) is a soft leash on one qualifying scout drone — a Personal or Light air frame tagged Recon, Mark, or Decoy.

As a maneuver, deploy that drone on the leash or issue one soft order: follow, watch, hold, scout, surveillance, or minor support (spot or mark, watch a corner, light carry if the chassis can). This is not a gun platform and not Jump-In.

Limits: max one drone active. The link lasts about one scene, then the drone standbys (~10 minutes / between scenes to reset). You may run one basic Pilot or Sensor program. Rigging and Gunnery-through-drone power rolls take a bane. You cannot use Fleet Deck+ features, Uptime, Deploy & Command, or Jump-In unless you are a Wrench using those class tools separately.

StreetEye.Granted: {actor} picked up a scout drone — Street Eye is on the sheet.
StreetEye.Revoked: {actor} has no qualifying scout drone — Street Eye is gone.

Taint.Label: Taint
Taint.Hint: Spiritual stain, 0–12. Rest never cleanses it. Chrome does not raise it. Owner and GM edit this number when the table awards or rites Taint.
Taint.BandHint: Band from Taint: Clean 0 · Marked 1–3 · Stained 4–6 · Claimed 7–9 · Hollowed 10–12.

History.Label: Corruption History
History.Hint: Fiction notes: how Taint was gained, visible tells, cleanses, pacts, and debts. Not a second meter.
History.Placeholder: How the stain landed, what it looks like, what you still owe…

Integrity.Label: Body Integrity
Integrity.Hint: Flesh left for chrome. Installing an implant spends its Integrity; removing it returns 75% (round down). Integrity doesn’t recover with rest.
Integrity.CyborgNA: Not used — Cyborgs upgrade with Frame Modules, not chrome.
Integrity.Insufficient: {actor} can’t install {name}: it needs {cost} Body Integrity and only {value} is left.
Integrity.CyborgBlocked: {actor} is a Cyborg and can’t install chrome implants like {name}. Cyborgs use Frame Modules.
Integrity.SlotFull: {actor} can’t install {name}: the {location} location already holds {count} of {cap} implants.

ArcaneSeverance.ClassBlocked: {actor} is a Cyborg: Arcane Severance bars all magic, so they can’t take the {name} class.
ArcaneSeverance.AncestryBlocked: {actor} is a {name}: Arcane Severance bars all magic, so they can’t become a Cyborg.

CasterChrome.SheetLineOver: Chrome spent {spent} / {cap} soft-cap — Weave Strain: bane on Magic / Veil / Resonance power rolls
CasterChrome.Hint: Caster chrome soft-cap: Elementalists, Street Priests, and Technomancers take a bane on every Magic, Veil, or Resonance power roll while more than 5 Body Integrity is spent on installed chrome. Removing implants to get back to 5 or less clears it. Magic erosion applies separately.
CasterChrome.Over: {actor} has {spent} Body Integrity spent on chrome, over the caster soft-cap of {cap}: Weave Strain — Magic / Veil / Resonance power rolls take a bane until chrome is removed.
CasterChrome.Cleared: {actor} is back to {spent} / {cap} Body Integrity spent on chrome: Weave Strain clears.

Effect.Name: Chrome Soft-Cap — Weave Strain
Effect.Description: More than 5 Body Integrity is spent on installed chrome. Every Magic, Veil, or Resonance power roll takes a bane until surgical removal brings spent Integrity back to 5 or less. Ghostwire adds and removes this effect automatically; disable it to waive the bane.

MagicErosion.SheetLineEroded: {resource} cap {cap} (base {base} − erosion {erosion}) — chrome is eroding your magic
MagicErosion.Breakdown: Magic erosion: Soft {soft} Integrity → −{softLoss} · Standard {standard} → −{standardLoss} · Salvage {salvage} → −{salvageLoss}. Base cap is 8 / 12 / 16 / 20 by echelon (Street Priest: +2 Burgeoning Saint / Rising Adept, +4 Most Faithful). Gains past the cap are lost.
MagicErosion.Clamped: {actor}'s casting resource is capped at {cap} by level and magic erosion; the excess is lost.

Datajack.Name: Datajack
Datajack.Description:
Grade: Standard · Location: Head / Neural · Body Integrity: 1 · Price: ¥500 · Availability: Street

A direct-neural port behind the ear or at the base of the skull. You can jack straight into the Wired and compatible devices without a manual interface — the decker and rigger baseline. Hacking and Wired rules that require a neural interface treat you as having one.

Install: drag onto a living (non-Cyborg) hero. Ghostwire spends 1 Body Integrity automatically and blocks the install if the hero doesn’t have enough Integrity or a free Head / Neural slot. Deleting the implant returns 75% of its Integrity (round down). Cyborgs can’t install chrome.
Datajack.EffectDescription: Wired interface: you have a direct neural connection to the Wired and compatible devices.

CyberEyes.Name: Cyber-Eyes
CyberEyes.Description:
Grade: Standard · Location: Eyes / Optics · Body Integrity: 2 · Price: ¥2,000 · Availability: Professional

An optical suite with low-light, thermal, magnification, and recording modes. You gain an edge on Perception tests (automated). You also ignore the bane from darkness or smoke on strikes (apply manually). Cyber-eyes are a discrete, destroyable target for called shots.

Install: drag onto a living (non-Cyborg) hero. Ghostwire spends 2 Body Integrity automatically and blocks the install if the hero doesn’t have enough Integrity or a free Eyes / Optics slot. Deleting the implant returns 75% of its Integrity (round down). Cyborgs can’t install chrome.
CyberEyes.EffectDescription: Edge on Perception tests. Ignore darkness or smoke banes on strikes (apply manually).

ReactionEnhancer.Name: Reaction Enhancer
ReactionEnhancer.Description:
Grade: Standard · Location: Nervous System · Body Integrity: 3 · Price: ¥3,500 · Availability: Restricted

A budget cousin of wired reflexes that shaves milliseconds off every reaction. When you take the Disengage move action, you can shift 1 additional square (automated). Nervous System holds one implant, so this can’t be combined with Wired Reflexes.

Install: drag onto a living (non-Cyborg) hero. Ghostwire spends 3 Body Integrity automatically and blocks the install if the hero doesn’t have enough Integrity or a free Nervous System slot. Deleting the implant returns 75% of its Integrity (round down). Cyborgs can’t install chrome.
ReactionEnhancer.EffectDescription: +1 square when you shift with Disengage.

DermalPlating.Name: Dermal Plating
DermalPlating.Description:
Grade: Standard · Location: Torso / Core · Body Integrity: 4 · Price: ¥4,000 · Availability: Restricted

Sub-dermal armor plates under the skin. You have damage immunity 2 against all damage (automated; provisional value). The plating is visibly chromed, which can cost you with people who distrust metal.

Install: drag onto a living (non-Cyborg) hero. Ghostwire spends 4 Body Integrity automatically and blocks the install if the hero doesn’t have enough Integrity or a free Torso / Core slot. Deleting the implant returns 75% of its Integrity (round down). Cyborgs can’t install chrome.

CyberlimbArm.Name: Cyberlimb (Arm)
CyberlimbArm.Description:
Grade: Standard · Location: Arms / Hands · Body Integrity: 5 · Price: ¥7,500 · Availability: Restricted

A full replacement arm with reinforced servos and a mounting point for integral tools or weapons. Your melee weapon abilities, including your melee free strike and unarmed Brawler or Mantis kit strikes, deal +1 damage on every power roll result (automated). A cyberlimb counts as the fists, blades, or grips that unarmed kits require. It is a large slot draw and a called-shot target.

Install: drag onto a living (non-Cyborg) hero. Ghostwire spends 5 Body Integrity automatically and blocks the install if the hero doesn’t have enough Integrity or a free Arms / Hands slot. Deleting the implant returns 75% of its Integrity (round down). Cyborgs can’t install chrome.
CyberlimbArm.EffectDescription: +1 damage on melee weapon abilities (all power roll results).

VocalModulator.Name: Vocal Modulator
VocalModulator.Description:
Grade: Standard · Location: Head / Neural · Body Integrity: 1 · Price: ¥800 · Availability: Professional

A laryngeal implant that reshapes pitch, timbre, and accent on command, or mimics a voice you’ve recorded. You gain an edge on Deception tests when your voice sells the lie (automated). Face chrome — a Soft/bioware version reads as less obviously artificial.

Install: drag onto a living (non-Cyborg) hero. Ghostwire spends 1 Body Integrity automatically and blocks the install if the hero doesn’t have enough Integrity or a free Head / Neural slot. Deleting the implant returns 75% of its Integrity (round down). Cyborgs can’t install chrome.

ImplantWeapon.Name: Implant Weapon (Spur)
ImplantWeapon.Description:
Grade: Standard · Location: Arms / Hands · Body Integrity: 1 · Price: ¥1,000 · Availability: Restricted

A retractable blade spur housed in the forearm. It is concealed until deployed and can’t be disarmed. Installing it grants the Spur Strike signature ability, which is removed again if the implant is deleted.

Install: drag onto a living (non-Cyborg) hero. Ghostwire spends 1 Body Integrity automatically and blocks the install if the hero doesn’t have enough Integrity or a free Arms / Hands slot. Deleting the implant returns 75% of its Integrity (round down). Cyborgs can’t install chrome.
ImplantWeapon.EffectDescription: Concealed, non-disarmable forearm spur. Grants Spur Strike.

InternalAir.Name: Internal Air / Filtration
InternalAir.Description:
Grade: Standard · Location: Torso / Core · Body Integrity: 2 · Price: ¥1,500 · Availability: Professional

Sealed filters and a reserve air bladder in the chest. You can hold your breath for up to 10 minutes and filter smoke, gas, and airborne toxins. You have poison immunity 2 (automated), and you gain an edge on tests to resist inhaled gases and toxins (apply manually).

Install: drag onto a living (non-Cyborg) hero. Ghostwire spends 2 Body Integrity automatically and blocks the install if the hero doesn’t have enough Integrity or a free Torso / Core slot. Deleting the implant returns 75% of its Integrity (round down). Cyborgs can’t install chrome.
InternalAir.EffectDescription: Poison immunity 2. Edge on tests to resist inhaled gases and toxins (manual).

CyberEars.Name: Cyber-Ears
CyberEars.Description:
Grade: Standard · Location: Ears / Aural · Body Integrity: 2 · Price: ¥1,800 · Availability: Professional

An audio suite with amplification, spatial tracking, dampers against sudden noise, and live translation. You gain an edge on Perception tests (automated). This doesn’t stack with the Perception edge from Cyber-Eyes.

Install: drag onto a living (non-Cyborg) hero. Ghostwire spends 2 Body Integrity automatically and blocks the install if the hero doesn’t have enough Integrity or a free Ears / Aural slot. Deleting the implant returns 75% of its Integrity (round down). Cyborgs can’t install chrome.
CyberEars.EffectDescription: Edge on Perception tests (doesn’t stack with Cyber-Eyes).

RunningGear.Name: Running Gear
RunningGear.Description:
Grade: Standard · Location: Legs / Locomotion · Body Integrity: 3 · Price: ¥2,500 · Availability: Professional

Reinforced leg actuators and shock-absorbing joints. Your speed increases by 1, and you gain an edge on Athletics tests (both automated; doesn’t stack with Muscle / Bone Lacing’s Athletics edge). This doesn’t stack with another speed bonus from chrome that serves the same purpose — take the better.

Install: drag onto a living (non-Cyborg) hero. Ghostwire spends 3 Body Integrity automatically and blocks the install if the hero doesn’t have enough Integrity or a free Legs / Locomotion slot. Deleting the implant returns 75% of its Integrity (round down). Cyborgs can’t install chrome.

Skillwires.Name: Skillwires / Encephalon
Skillwires.Description:
Grade: Standard · Location: Head / Neural · Body Integrity: 4 · Price: ¥5,000 · Availability: Restricted

A skillsoft socket and co-processor that loads expertise directly into muscle memory. The default skillsoft gives an edge on Repair tests (automated). To load a different skillsoft, edit this implant’s effect and change the skill in the key (for example system.skills.modifiers.hacking.edges). Neural chrome erodes magic heavily.

Install: drag onto a living (non-Cyborg) hero. Ghostwire spends 4 Body Integrity automatically and blocks the install if the hero doesn’t have enough Integrity or a free Head / Neural slot. Deleting the implant returns 75% of its Integrity (round down). Cyborgs can’t install chrome.
Skillwires.EffectDescription: Loaded skillsoft: edge on Repair tests (edit the effect key to swap the skill).

MuscleBoneLacing.Name: Muscle / Bone Lacing
MuscleBoneLacing.Description:
Grade: Standard · Location: Torso / Core · Body Integrity: 5 · Price: ¥6,000 · Availability: Restricted

Synthetic muscle bundles and ceramic-laced bone. Your stability increases by 1, and you gain an edge on Athletics tests (both automated; doesn’t stack with Running Gear’s Athletics edge). Heavy Integrity draw.

Install: drag onto a living (non-Cyborg) hero. Ghostwire spends 5 Body Integrity automatically and blocks the install if the hero doesn’t have enough Integrity or a free Torso / Core slot. Deleting the implant returns 75% of its Integrity (round down). Cyborgs can’t install chrome.

WiredReflexes.Name: Wired Reflexes
WiredReflexes.Description:
Grade: Standard · Location: Nervous System · Body Integrity: 6 · Price: ¥12,000 · Availability: Military

Military-grade neural boosters that fire your body before you finish deciding to move. Your speed increases by 1, and you can shift 2 additional squares when you take the Disengage move action (both automated). When the Director checks which side acts first, the Director can count you as alert even when you’d otherwise be surprised (Director’s call). Nervous System holds one implant, so this can’t be combined with a Reaction Enhancer.

Install: drag onto a living (non-Cyborg) hero. Ghostwire spends 6 Body Integrity automatically and blocks the install if the hero doesn’t have enough Integrity or a free Nervous System slot. Deleting the implant returns 75% of its Integrity (round down). Cyborgs can’t install chrome.
WiredReflexes.EffectDescription: +1 speed. +2 squares when you shift with Disengage.

SpurStrike.Name: Spur Strike
SpurStrike.Story: A blade snaps out of your forearm and back in before anyone sees it.
SpurStrike.Effect: Your spur is concealed until it strikes and can’t be disarmed. If the target didn’t know you had an implant weapon, you have an edge on this strike.

CyberEyesSoft.Name: Cyber-Eyes (Soft)
CyberEyesSoft.Description:
Grade: Soft · Location: Eyes / Optics · Body Integrity: 1 · Price: ¥8,000 · Availability: Restricted

Vat-grown replacement eyes — cultured retina, living lens, a low-light and thermal-sensitive layer grown into the tissue rather than bolted behind it. They look like your own eyes on a good day. You gain an edge on Perception tests (automated) and ignore the bane from darkness or smoke on strikes (apply manually). Still a destroyable target for called shots.

Soft / Bioware: grown, not bolted. A Veil caster loses 1 point of casting-resource cap per 3 Body Integrity spent on Soft-grade chrome (Standard is per 2), so a single 1-Integrity Soft implant costs a caster no cap on its own (apply manually). Soft still counts toward the caster chrome soft-cap of 5 Body Integrity spent; above it, every Magic / Veil / Resonance power roll takes a bane.

Install: drag onto a living (non-Cyborg) hero. Ghostwire spends 1 Body Integrity automatically and blocks the install if the hero doesn’t have enough Integrity or a free Eyes / Optics slot. Deleting the implant returns 75% of its Integrity (round down). Cyborgs can’t install chrome.
CyberEyesSoft.EffectDescription: Edge on Perception tests. Ignore darkness or smoke banes on strikes (apply manually).

CyberEarsSoft.Name: Cyber-Ears (Soft)
CyberEarsSoft.Description:
Grade: Soft · Location: Ears / Aural · Body Integrity: 1 · Price: ¥7,200 · Availability: Restricted

A cultured cochlear lattice grown into the inner ear: amplification, spatial tracking and a reflex damper against sudden noise, with nothing to see from outside. You gain an edge on Perception tests (automated). This doesn’t stack with the Perception edge from any Cyber-Eyes.

Soft / Bioware: grown, not bolted. A Veil caster loses 1 point of casting-resource cap per 3 Body Integrity spent on Soft-grade chrome (Standard is per 2), so a single 1-Integrity Soft implant costs a caster no cap on its own (apply manually). Soft still counts toward the caster chrome soft-cap of 5 Body Integrity spent; above it, every Magic / Veil / Resonance power roll takes a bane.

Install: drag onto a living (non-Cyborg) hero. Ghostwire spends 1 Body Integrity automatically and blocks the install if the hero doesn’t have enough Integrity or a free Ears / Aural slot. Deleting the implant returns 75% of its Integrity (round down). Cyborgs can’t install chrome.
CyberEarsSoft.EffectDescription: Edge on Perception tests (doesn’t stack with Cyber-Eyes).

VocalModulatorSoft.Name: Vocal Modulator (Soft)
VocalModulatorSoft.Description:
Grade: Soft · Location: Head / Neural · Body Integrity: 1 · Price: ¥3,200 · Availability: Restricted

Tailored vocal cords and a grown laryngeal muscle sheath that reshape pitch, timbre and accent, or mimic a voice you’ve studied. No scar, no hum, no tell. You gain an edge on Deception tests when your voice sells the lie (automated). The Face’s preferred grade — it reads as talent, not hardware.

Soft / Bioware: grown, not bolted. A Veil caster loses 1 point of casting-resource cap per 3 Body Integrity spent on Soft-grade chrome (Standard is per 2), so a single 1-Integrity Soft implant costs a caster no cap on its own (apply manually). Soft still counts toward the caster chrome soft-cap of 5 Body Integrity spent; above it, every Magic / Veil / Resonance power roll takes a bane.

Install: drag onto a living (non-Cyborg) hero. Ghostwire spends 1 Body Integrity automatically and blocks the install if the hero doesn’t have enough Integrity or a free Head / Neural slot. Deleting the implant returns 75% of its Integrity (round down). Cyborgs can’t install chrome.

DatajackSoft.Name: Datajack (Soft Neural Lace)
DatajackSoft.Description:
Grade: Soft · Location: Head / Neural · Body Integrity: 1 · Price: ¥2,000 · Availability: Professional

A cultured neural lace grown along the brainstem, surfacing as a soft contact patch under the hairline instead of a metal port. You can jack straight into the Wired and compatible devices without a manual interface. Hacking and Wired rules that require a neural interface treat you as having one.

Soft / Bioware: grown, not bolted. A Veil caster loses 1 point of casting-resource cap per 3 Body Integrity spent on Soft-grade chrome (Standard is per 2), so a single 1-Integrity Soft implant costs a caster no cap on its own (apply manually). Soft still counts toward the caster chrome soft-cap of 5 Body Integrity spent; above it, every Magic / Veil / Resonance power roll takes a bane.

Install: drag onto a living (non-Cyborg) hero. Ghostwire spends 1 Body Integrity automatically and blocks the install if the hero doesn’t have enough Integrity or a free Head / Neural slot. Deleting the implant returns 75% of its Integrity (round down). Cyborgs can’t install chrome.
DatajackSoft.EffectDescription: Wired interface: you have a direct neural connection to the Wired and compatible devices.

EmpathyProcessorSoft.Name: Empathy Processor (Soft)
EmpathyProcessorSoft.Description:
Grade: Soft · Location: Head / Neural · Body Integrity: 1 · Price: ¥4,000 · Availability: Restricted

A grown cluster of mirror-neuron tissue that reads micro-expressions, pulse in the throat and the stress in a voice, and feeds you the answer as a gut feeling. Horizon Persona sells it Soft-grade only, as part of the Silvertongue social line. You gain an edge on Insight tests (automated).

Soft / Bioware: grown, not bolted. A Veil caster loses 1 point of casting-resource cap per 3 Body Integrity spent on Soft-grade chrome (Standard is per 2), so a single 1-Integrity Soft implant costs a caster no cap on its own (apply manually). Soft still counts toward the caster chrome soft-cap of 5 Body Integrity spent; above it, every Magic / Veil / Resonance power roll takes a bane.

Install: drag onto a living (non-Cyborg) hero. Ghostwire spends 1 Body Integrity automatically and blocks the install if the hero doesn’t have enough Integrity or a free Head / Neural slot. Deleting the implant returns 75% of its Integrity (round down). Cyborgs can’t install chrome.

PheromoneGlandSoft.Name: Tailored Pheromone Gland (Soft)
PheromoneGlandSoft.Description:
Grade: Soft · Location: Torso / Core · Body Integrity: 1 · Price: ¥5,000 · Availability: Restricted

A small cultured gland tuned to your chemistry that releases a trust-and-warmth signature when you choose to be liked. People lean in without knowing why. Horizon Persona sells it Soft-grade only, as part of the Silvertongue social line. You gain an edge on Persuasion tests (automated). Filtration masks and sealed environments shut it off (apply manually).

Soft / Bioware: grown, not bolted. A Veil caster loses 1 point of casting-resource cap per 3 Body Integrity spent on Soft-grade chrome (Standard is per 2), so a single 1-Integrity Soft implant costs a caster no cap on its own (apply manually). Soft still counts toward the caster chrome soft-cap of 5 Body Integrity spent; above it, every Magic / Veil / Resonance power roll takes a bane.

Install: drag onto a living (non-Cyborg) hero. Ghostwire spends 1 Body Integrity automatically and blocks the install if the hero doesn’t have enough Integrity or a free Torso / Core slot. Deleting the implant returns 75% of its Integrity (round down). Cyborgs can’t install chrome.
PheromoneGlandSoft.EffectDescription: Edge on Persuasion tests. No effect on targets behind filtration masks or in sealed environments (apply manually).

Longshot.Name: Longshot
Longshot.Description:
Rooftop overwatch and one-shot problem solving. Longshots trade mobility for distance and a huge payoff when the shot lands clean.

Gear category: Precision rifle; no armor

Ownership rule: this Kit is inert without its gear. You must own a qualifying item — bought with ¥ and Availability-gated — to use its bonuses. No qualifying weapon in hand means no weapon bonuses and no Kit signature ability (you’re using an improvised weapon). No qualifying armor worn means no Stamina or stability bonus. Kit doctrine is training and never costs ¥.

Doctrine bonuses (provisional, Draw Steel Sniper benchmark): Speed +1 · Disengage +1 · Ranged damage +0/+0/+4 · Ranged distance +10. Damage is listed low / middle / high result.

Signature ability: @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.kits.Item.eyTvU2KKgnfr6dM1]{Held Breath}

Signature.Name: Held Breath
Signature.Story: Breathe … settle the reticle … wait … then squeeze.
Signature.Effect: If you don’t take a move action this turn, this strike deals extra damage equal to [[lookup @chr]]{your Physique or Reflex score (your choice)}.

Saturation.Name: Saturation
Saturation.Description:
Volume of fire wins arguments. Saturation runners keep two targets’ heads down at once.

Improved Cyberdeck (4th level) and Root Access (9th level) add to both. A cyberdeck is not a weapon Kit: it grants no Stamina, speed, or weapon damage.

Signature ability: @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.kits.Item.TsxYhiFWjcsNut2K]{Overwatch Ping}

Signature.Name: Overwatch Ping
Signature.Story: Real-time Wired data, fed to a crewmate.
Signature.Effect: Feed one ally within Reach real-time Wired data. No damage.
Signature.Tier1: The ally gains an edge on their next power roll before the end of your next turn; Trace Alert increases.
Signature.Tier2: The ally gains an edge on their next power roll before the end of your next turn.
Signature.Tier3: The ally gains an edge on their next power roll, and you learn one enemy position they can’t see.

ControlledPair.Name: Controlled Pair
ControlledPair.Story: Two aimed shots, center mass, before they can blink.

SuppressingFire.Name: Suppressing Fire
SuppressingFire.Story: You hose down a zone to keep heads low and pin enemies in place.

BreachAndClear.Name: Breach & Clear
BreachAndClear.Effect_after00000000000: If you or an ally moves into a square the target vacated this turn, an opportunity attack that creature would have taken against you or that ally targets the slid target instead.
BreachAndClear.Story: Put them where you want them, then take the space they left.

TriggerCadence.Name: Trigger Cadence
TriggerCadence.Effect_before0000000000: You gain 1 surge, and the next ability power roll you make this turn automatically obtains a high (17+) outcome.
TriggerCadence.Story: Breathe. Squeeze. Your nervous system does the rest.

HoldTheLine.Name: Hold the Line
HoldTheLine.Trigger: An enemy moves adjacent to you or within 3 squares of you.

Overwatch.Name: Overwatch
Overwatch.Effect_after00000000000: You can use this ability against each enemy only once per encounter.
Overwatch.Story: You’ve had the lane covered since before they walked into it.
Overwatch.Trigger: An enemy within distance moves or uses an action for the first time this encounter.

AdrenalineDump.Name: Adrenaline Dump
AdrenalineDump.Effect_after00000000000: For one target, you can take [[/damage 1d6]]{1d6 damage} to deal an extra [[/damage 1d6]]{1d6 damage} to that target.
AdrenalineDump.Story: Everything you’ve got, all at once.

Class.Name: Operator
Class.Description:
You are an Operator — a street samurai, edgerunner, or professional shooter who fights with chrome, discipline, and a body wired to run hotter than anyone else on the field. You don’t hack the Wired and you don’t burn magic; you close distance, put rounds and blades where they count, and keep coming back for more when everyone else would already be down.

Whether you’re a Corp-Milspec asset running fire-team doctrine, a Merc carrying two kits into every job, or a Street-vet who survived the gutter long enough to become a professional, your identity is the same: chrome-forward, casts nothing, and dangerous specifically because you do not stop.

Core characteristics: Physique, Reflex · Heroic resource: Adrenaline · Starting Stamina: 21 (+9 per level) · Recoveries: 10 · Kit: yes (Merc carries two).

Adrenaline.Name: Adrenaline
Adrenaline.Description:
Adrenaline in Combat. At the start of a combat encounter (or any other tense situation the Director tracks in combat rounds), you gain Adrenaline equal to your Victories. At the start of each of your turns during combat, you gain 1d3 Adrenaline. Additionally, the first time each combat round that you take damage, you gain 1 Adrenaline. The first time you become winded or are dying in an encounter, you gain 1d3 Adrenaline. You lose any remaining Adrenaline at the end of the encounter.

Adrenaline Outside of Combat. You can’t gain Adrenaline outside of combat, but you can still use your heroic abilities and effects that cost Adrenaline without spending it. Whenever you use an ability or effect outside of combat that costs Adrenaline, you can’t use that same ability or effect outside of combat again until you earn 1 or more Victories or finish a respite. When you use an ability outside of combat that lets you spend unlimited Adrenaline on its effect, you can use it as if you had spent an amount of Adrenaline equal to your Victories.

Growing Adrenaline. You gain certain benefits in combat based on the amount of Adrenaline you currently have (see your Origin’s Growing Adrenaline table). These benefits last until the end of your turn, even if a benefit would become unavailable because you spent Adrenaline during that turn.

ChromeUnleashed.Name: Chrome Unleashed
ChromeUnleashed.Story: Foes tremble at the sight of you.
ChromeUnleashed.Effect_before0000000000: Until the end of the encounter or until you are dying, each enemy who starts their turn adjacent to you and has [[potency P strong]] is [[/apply frightened turn]] until the end of their turn.

FaceTheHail.Name: Face the Hail
FaceTheHail.Story: Shocked in the face of your naked brutality, your enemy’s instincts take over.
FaceTheHail.Effect_before0000000000: Until the end of the encounter or until you are dying, each creature you make a melee strike against who has [[potency p average]] is taunted until the end of their next turn. Additionally, when you use an ability that deals rolled damage against any enemy taunted by you, the ability deals [[/damage 2*@M]]{extra damage} equal to twice your Physique score and increases its potency by 1.

ArmorBreaker.Name: Armor Breaker
ArmorBreaker.Story: See how useless their weapons are!

AlreadyFlatlined.Name: Already Flatlined
AlreadyFlatlined.Effect_before0000000000: If the target is not a leader or solo creature, they are reduced to 0 Stamina at the end of their next turn. If the target is a leader or solo creature, you [[/surge 3]] and can make a melee free strike against them.

CripplingBurst.Name: Crippling Burst
CripplingBurst.Story: You need just one blow to sabotage your target.
CripplingBurst.Effect_after00000000000: While slowed this way, the target takes 1 damage for every square they move, including from forced movement.

MyMove.Name: My Move!
MyMove.Story: You quickly strike back at a foe.
MyMove.Trigger: A creature causes you to be winded or dying, or damages you while you are winded or dying.

ReboundingFire.Name: Rebounding Fire
ReboundingFire.Story: You knock around enemies like playthings.
ReboundingFire.Effect_after00000000000: When a target would end this forced movement by colliding with a creature or object, they take damage as usual, then are pushed the remaining distance away from the creature or object in the direction they came from. As long as forced movement remains, this effect continues if the target collides with another creature or object.

LockDown.Name: Lock Down!
LockDown.Story: Your strikes overload the target’s nervous system until their body simply stops answering.
LockDown.Effect_after00000000000: While the target is slowed this way, any other effect that would make the target slowed instead makes them [[/apply Restrained]] by this ability. Additionally, a creature who fails the saving throw while restrained this way is locked down — [[/apply Petrified]] — until they receive specialist medical attention or you choose to reverse the effect (no action required).

OverclockedAdrenaline.Name: Overclocked Adrenaline
OverclockedAdrenaline.Story: Your overclocked nervous system turns every hit you take into instant retribution.
OverclockedAdrenaline.Effect_before0000000000: You gain [[/heal 10 temp]]. Additionally, choose acid, cold, corruption, fire, lightning, poison, or sonic damage. Until the end of the encounter or until you are dying, whenever an enemy damages you, they take [[/damage 10 type=acid/cold/corruption/fire/lightning/poison/sonic]] damage of the chosen type. If this damage reduces the enemy to 0 Stamina, you gain [[/heal 10 temp]].

Overkill.Name: Overkill
Overkill.Story: You strike so no damage is wasted.
Overkill.Effect_after00000000000: If the target is a minion or is winded but isn’t a leader or solo creature, they are reduced to 0 Stamina before this ability’s damage is dealt. If the target is killed by this damage, you can deal any damage over what was required to kill them to another creature within 5 squares of the target.

CombatTrance.Name: Combat Trance
CombatTrance.Story: The world slows down, and your Adrenaline turns into pure violence.
CombatTrance.Effect_before0000000000: Choose acid, cold, corruption, fire, lightning, poison, or sonic damage. Until the end of the encounter or until you are dying, you can choose one target of any ability you use, with that target taking an extra [[/damage 15 type=acid/cold/corruption/fire/lightning/poison/sonic]] damage of the chosen type. Additionally, whenever you gain Adrenaline from taking damage, the source of the damage takes [[/damage 5 type=acid/cold/corruption/fire/lightning/poison/sonic]] damage of the chosen type.

Relentless.Name: Relentless
Relentless.Effect_before0000000000: You shift up to your speed. Each enemy you move adjacent to during this movement takes [[/damage 2*@M]]{damage equal to twice your Physique score}. Then make one power roll that targets each enemy you move adjacent to during this shift. You [[/gain 1 heroic]]{gain 1 Adrenaline} for each target who dies as a result of this ability (maximum 11 Adrenaline).

DamagingAdrenaline.Name: Damaging Adrenaline
DamagingAdrenaline.Description: The first time you take damage each combat round, you gain 2 Adrenaline instead of 1.

GrowingAdrenalineI.Name: Growing Adrenaline I
GrowingAdrenalineI.Description: Your Growing Adrenaline feature provides additional benefits when you have 8 or more Adrenaline.

CombatAttunement.Name: Combat Attunement
CombatAttunement.Description: Combat-grade sensors and hard-won instinct tell you how damage interacts with everyone around you. You automatically sense whether any creature within 10 squares has damage immunity or damage weakness to acid, cold, corruption, fire, lightning, poison, or sonic damage, learning whether they have immunity or weakness, its value, and the damage type. Additionally, you automatically sense any source of one of those damage types within 10 squares, such as a fire, a live cable, or a chemical spill.

PrecisionStrike.Name: Precision Strike
PrecisionStrike.Description: You channel your Adrenaline into a perfectly placed hit. As part of any strike, you can spend 1 Adrenaline to [[/surge 1]] that must be used for that strike. The extra damage dealt by the surge can be acid, cold, corruption, fire, lightning, poison, or sonic (your choice) — the round, blade, or charge you loaded for it.

VeteranOfTheSprawl.Name: Veteran of the Sprawl
VeteranOfTheSprawl.Description: You passively detect security systems, drones, and Corp-Milspec presence within 1 mile, and you read corp and gang signal traffic fluently. Treat your Renown as 1 higher with corp and gang contacts. The first time a Corp-Milspec operative becomes aware of you, they are frightened of you until the end of the encounter if they have Persona lower than your average potency.

BreachPoint.Name: Breach Point
BreachPoint.Description:
A breach point is a standing, reusable tear you personally open between the physical world and the deep network — a hidden, secured layer of the Wired reachable only through a breach point and anchored on your end to a live relay node (a node you or an ally has set up and is actively maintaining; see Ghost of the Sprawl).

As a main action, touch a live relay node to open a breach point into the deep network. You can then spend a main action to route yourself and any willing creatures within 10 squares of you through the breach onto a secured safehouse node, or to route back the same way. You can maintain a number of breach points equal to your Physique score, and every breach point you hold leads to the same safehouse node. If a breach point is destroyed, it drops out of your network; you can remove one voluntarily at any distance, no action required. Exploring the deep network beyond your safehouse node is possible, but safety there isn’t guaranteed.

CombatForm.Name: Combat Form
CombatForm.Description:
Your chrome and nervous system show the strain of how hot you run. Whenever you show strong emotion or increase your Adrenaline, your chrome flares — heat shimmer, static, or a visible glow in your implants.

Additionally, if you are a Corp-Milspec or Merc, you have immunity to acid, cold, corruption, fire, lightning, poison, and sonic damage equal to [[lookup @M]]{your Physique score}. If you are a Street-vet, you have immunity to your loadout damage type equal to [[lookup 2*@M evaluate=true]]{twice your Physique score}.

GreaterAdrenaline.Name: Greater Adrenaline
GreaterAdrenaline.Description: When you gain Adrenaline at the start of each of your turns during combat, you gain 1d3 + 1 Adrenaline instead of 1d3.

GrowingAdrenalineII.Name: Growing Adrenaline II
GrowingAdrenalineII.Description: Your Growing Adrenaline feature provides additional benefits when you have 10 or more Adrenaline.

GhostOfTheSprawl.Name: Ghost of the Sprawl
GhostOfTheSprawl.Description: As a respite activity, you establish a temporary secured relay node that lasts 24 hours. You can use it with your Breach Point feature to open a breach point into the deep network; if you do, the relay node persists as long as you maintain that breach point.

WarzoneIncarnate.Name: Warzone Incarnate
WarzoneIncarnate.Description:
You’ve walked through every kind of fire the Sprawl can throw. If you are a Corp-Milspec or Merc, you have immunity to acid, cold, corruption, fire, lightning, poison, and sonic damage equal to [[lookup 2*@M evaluate=true]]{twice your Physique score}. If you are a Street-vet, your immunity to your loadout damage type increases to [[lookup 3*@M evaluate=true]]{three times your Physique score}.

When any creature whose abilities deal acid, cold, corruption, fire, lightning, poison, or sonic damage first becomes aware of you in combat, if they have [[potency P strong]], they are [[/apply frightened save]].

Additionally, when you use Precision Strike, you can spend up to 3 Adrenaline, [[/surge 1]]{gaining 1 surge} per Adrenaline spent to use for that strike.
WarzoneIncarnate.Director: This feature is an upgrade of the effects granted by the 7th level feature “Combat Form.” You can increase the values of the effect you already have to match the values of this feature.

GrowingAdrenalineIII.Name: Growing Adrenaline III
GrowingAdrenalineIII.Description: Your Growing Adrenaline feature provides additional benefits when you have 12 or more Adrenaline.

PeakAdrenaline.Name: Peak Adrenaline
PeakAdrenaline.Description: The first time you take damage each combat round, you gain 3 Adrenaline instead of 2.

OperatorMastery.Name: Operator Mastery
OperatorMastery.Description: You gain an epic resource called Overclock. Each time you finish a respite, you gain Overclock equal to the XP you gain. You can spend Overclock on your abilities as if it were Adrenaline. You can also spend any amount of Overclock as a free maneuver to end one effect on you per Overclock spent, and you can spend 3 Overclock to open a breach point into the deep network without needing a live relay node. Overclock remains until you spend it.

CorpMilspec.Name: Corp-Milspec
CorpMilspec.Description:
“Company Asset.” Fire-team doctrine drilled into you by a corporate or military program: breaching, controlling space, and hitting hard enough to move people.

At 1st level you gain the Command skill and choose one Kit.

BreachingForce.Name: Breaching Force
BreachingForce.Description:
Whenever you damage an object with a weapon strike, the strike deals extra damage equal to [[lookup @M]]{your Physique score}. Additionally, whenever you push another creature into an object, the creature takes extra damage equal to [[lookup @M]]{your Physique score}.

As your Adrenaline grows, you gain benefits as noted on the @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.classes.Item.3t5oRaCIWuHaazPt]{Corp-Milspec Growing Adrenaline} table. Benefits are cumulative except where an improved benefit replaces a lesser benefit.

GrowingAdrenalineCorpMilspec.Name: Growing Adrenaline
GrowingAdrenalineCorpMilspec.Description:
You gain certain benefits in combat based on the amount of Adrenaline you have. These benefits last until the end of your turn, even if a benefit would become unavailable to you because of the amount of Adrenaline you spend during your turn. Some Growing Adrenaline benefits can be applied only if you are a specific level or higher, with the level of those benefits noted in the various Growing Adrenaline tables in this section.

Adrenaline

Benefit

2

Whenever you use the Knockback maneuver, the forced movement distance gains a bonus equal to [[lookup @M]]{your Physique score}.

4

The first time you push a creature on a turn, you [[/surge 1]].

6

You gain an edge on Physique tests and the Knockback maneuver

8 (4th Level)

The first time you push a creature on a turn, you [[/surge 2]].

10 (7th Level)

You have a double edge on Physique tests and the Knockback maneuver.

12 (10th Level)

Whenever you use a heroic ability, you gain [[/heal 10 temporary]]. Additionally, whenever you make a power roll that imposes forced movement on a target, the forced movement distance gains a bonus equal to [[lookup @M]]{your Physique score}.

KineticRedirect.Name: Kinetic Redirect
KineticRedirect.Story: You redirect the energy of motion.
KineticRedirect.Trigger: The target would be force moved
KineticRedirect.Effect_spend00000000000: The forced movement distance gains a bonus equal to twice your Physique score instead.
KineticRedirect.Effect_before0000000000: You can select a new target of the same size or smaller within distance to be force moved instead. You become the source of the forced movement, determine the new target’s destination, and can push the target instead of using the original forced movement type. Additionally, the forced movement distance gains a bonus equal to [[lookup @M]]{your Physique score}.

BreachCharge.Name: Breach Charge
BreachCharge.Description: Whenever you use the @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel.abilities.Item.wNqJWJbgAbnJBqZf]{Charge} main action, you can use a strike signature ability or a strike heroic ability instead of a free strike. Additionally, you can jump as part of your charge.

DangerClose.Name: Danger Close
DangerClose.Effect_before0000000000: You vertically push the target up to 4 squares. This forced movement ignores the target’s stability, and the target takes no damage from colliding with creatures or objects. At the end of this movement, the target can make a free strike that deals extra damage equal to [[lookup @M]]{your Physique score}.

DemolitionSwing.Name: Demolition Swing
DemolitionSwing.Story: It’s easier to destroy than to create. Much easier, in fact!
DemolitionSwing.Effect_before0000000000:
You move up to your speed in a straight line. During this movement, you can move through mundane structures, including walls, which are difficult terrain for you. You automatically destroy each square of structure you move through and leave behind a square of difficult terrain.

Additionally, you make one power roll that targets each enemy you move adjacent to during this movement.

AnchoredStance.Name: Anchored Stance
AnchoredStance.Description:
You add your level to your effective size for the purpose of interacting with creatures and objects, including determining whether you can lift an object, are affected by forced movement, and so forth. This has no effect on whether you can be grabbed.

Additionally, you have a bonus to stability equal to [[lookup @M]]{your Physique score}.

JumpRig.Name: Jump Rig
JumpRig.Description: Your jump distance and height double. Additionally, when you fall, you reduce the effective height of your fall by a number of squares equal to your jump distance for the purpose of determining damage and whether you land prone. You are not prone after falling and landing on another creature.

OrbitalDrop.Name: Orbital Drop
OrbitalDrop.Story: You leap and crash down, causing a shockwave that devastates foes.
OrbitalDrop.Effect_before0000000000: You jump up to your maximum jump distance and make one power roll that targets each creature adjacent to the space where you land.

ConcussiveThrow.Name: Concussive Throw
ConcussiveThrow.Story: You strike an enemy hard enough to be a projectile that knocks a crowd of creatures around.
ConcussiveThrow.Effect_after00000000000: When the target ends this forced movement, each creature within 2 squares of the target is pushed 3 squares.

OverpoweringBuild.Name: Overpowering Build
OverpoweringBuild.Description: Your strength is unmatched. Whenever you make a Physique test, you can roll three dice and choose which two to use. Additionally, whenever you use the Knockback maneuver, the forced movement distance gains a bonus equal to [[lookup @M]]{your Physique score}.

FireForEffect.Name: Fire For Effect
FireForEffect.Story: You use your weapon to create a destructive shockwave.
FireForEffect.Effect_after00000000000: If this forced movement causes a target to be hurled through an object, that target takes an extra [[/damage 10]].

GravityWellCharge.Name: Gravity Well Charge
GravityWellCharge.Story: A shaped gravitic charge detonates and drags everyone toward you.
GravityWellCharge.Effect_after00000000000: If this forced movement causes a target to slam into you, you take no damage from the collision and the target takes the damage you would have taken.

Merc.Name: Merc
Merc.Description:
“Free Company Veteran.” Field Arsenal training — the only Origin that maintains two Kits at once — built on staying a step ahead of the job and the people paying for it.

At 1st level you gain the Demolitions skill and choose two Kits (see Field Arsenal).

CombatInstinct.Name: Combat Instinct
CombatInstinct.Description:
You are never surprised. Additionally, whenever you would push a target with forced movement, you can slide them instead.

As your Adrenaline grows, you gain benefits as noted on the @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.classes.Item.ieGJV4l66nywzuxo]{Merc Growing Adrenaline} table. Benefits are cumulative except where an improved benefit replaces a lesser benefit.

GrowingAdrenalineMerc.Name: Growing Adrenaline
GrowingAdrenalineMerc.Description:
You gain certain benefits in combat based on the amount of Adrenaline you have. These benefits last until the end of your turn, even if a benefit would become unavailable to you because of the amount of Adrenaline you spend during your turn. Some Growing Adrenaline benefits can be applied only if you are a specific level or higher, with the level of those benefits noted in the various Growing Adrenaline tables in this section.

Adrenaline

Benefit

2

Whenever you use the Knockback maneuver, the forced movement distance gains a bonus equal to [[lookup @A]]{your Reflex score}.

4

The first time you slide a creature on a turn, you [[/surge 1]].

6

You gain an edge on Reflex tests and the Knockback maneuver

8 (4th Level)

The first time you slide a creature on a turn, you [[/surge 2]].

10 (7th Level)

You have a double edge on Reflex tests and the Knockback maneuver.

12 (10th Level)

Whenever you use a heroic ability, you gain [[/heal 10 temporary]]. Additionally, whenever you make a power roll that imposes forced movement on a target, the forced movement distance gains a bonus equal to [[lookup @A]]{your Reflex score}.

WiredReflexes.Name: Wired Reflexes
WiredReflexes.Story: Your boosted nervous system moves you before the hit fully lands.
WiredReflexes.Effect_spend00000000000: If the damage has any potency effects associated with it, the potency is reduced by 1 for you.
WiredReflexes.Effect_before0000000000: You take half the damage from the triggering effect and can shift up to a number of squares equal to [[lookup @A]]{your Reflex score}.

RunAndGun.Name: Run and Gun
RunAndGun.Description: You have a bonus to speed equal to [[lookup @A]]{your Reflex score}, and you ignore difficult terrain.

SuppressionKill.Name: Suppression Kill
SuppressionKill.Story: Your controlled violence strikes terror into everyone watching.

FormationBreaker.Name: Formation Breaker
FormationBreaker.Story: Organizing your forces like feckless creatures of Law. Pitiful.
FormationBreaker.Effect_before0000000000: You shift up to your speed and make one power roll that targets up to three enemies you move adjacent to during this shift.

ReadTheMark.Name: Read the Mark
ReadTheMark.Description: You have a double edge on tests made to search for hidden creatures, discern hidden motives, or detect lies. You also have a double edge on tests made to gamble!

SlipTheCuffs.Name: Slip the Cuffs
SlipTheCuffs.Description: At the start of your turn, you can end any restrained condition on you. Additionally, you have a double edge on tests made to escape being confined or imprisoned.

ContractFulfilled.Name: Contract Fulfilled
ContractFulfilled.Story: Once the first target drops, you get efficient — every kill is a chance to line up the next.
ContractFulfilled.Trigger: You reduce a creature to 0 Stamina with a strike.
ContractFulfilled.Effect_before0000000000: You target a creature adjacent to you with the same strike, using the same power roll as the triggering strike.

BreachTheLine.Name: Breach the Line
BreachTheLine.Story: You break through the enemy lines to make an example.
BreachTheLine.Effect_after00000000000: If a target who is not a leader or solo creature is winded by this strike, they are reduced to 0 Stamina and you choose an enemy within 5 squares of you. If that enemy has [[potency P average]], they are [[/apply frightened save]].

AlwaysMoving.Name: Always Moving
AlwaysMoving.Description: You move with legendary grace. Whenever you make an Reflex test, you can roll three dice and choose which two to use. Additionally, whenever you use the Disengage move action, the distance you can shift gains a bonus equal to [[lookup @A]]{your Reflex score}.

TargetMarked.Name: Target Marked
TargetMarked.Story: You attune the target to be weaker to a specific element.
TargetMarked.Effect_after00000000000:
Choose acid, cold, corruption, fire, lightning, poison, or sonic damage. The target loses any damage immunity to the chosen type and gains weakness 10 to the chosen type (save ends).

[[/apply MGQmrgFa7IchnX8z]] [[/apply Z25OIEpHpelUvKWe]] [[/apply Tp4YLa282D8CY9eX]] [[/apply GZkQv6kUtb5gccNI]] [[/apply 2SJ7L3LBeALSQ4JA]] [[/apply d12CIjzP0dulOpUI]] [[/apply twQIogmZMlG19c4n]]

ShockAndAwe.Name: Shock and Awe
ShockAndAwe.Story: You shock your foes with the brutality of your strike, resetting the balance of combat.
ShockAndAwe.Effect_after00000000000: Each enemy within 5 squares of you is distracted until the end of the round. While a creature is distracted this way, they can’t take triggered actions or free triggered actions, ability rolls made against them gain an edge, and their characteristic scores are considered 1 lower for the purpose of resisting potencies.

StreetVet.Name: Street-vet
StreetVet.Description:
“Self-Made Killer.” Gutter Instinct training — you survived the street long enough to turn it into a profession, and you can’t be caught flat-footed.

At 1st level you gain the Intimidation skill, choose one Kit, and choose your loadout damage type: cryo (cold), toxin (corruption), incendiary (fire), or shock (lightning). Street-vet abilities and features that refer to your loadout damage type use it.

GutterInstinct.Name: Gutter Instinct
GutterInstinct.Description: You can’t be surprised. Once per encounter when you are hit by a strike, you can turn that hit into a glancing blow: you take half the damage (round down) and gain 1 Adrenaline.

OverclockNerves.Name: Overclock Nerves
OverclockNerves.Story: Pain spikes, your nerves overclock, and your body stops listening to it.
OverclockNerves.Trigger: You lose Stamina and are not dying.
OverclockNerves.Effect_spend00000000000: if you are not dying, you can spend a Recovery.
OverclockNerves.Effect_before0000000000: You gain [[/heal @M temp]]{temporary Stamina} equal to your Physique score as your nerves overclock and pain stops registering.

SurvivorsNose.Name: Survivor’s Nose
SurvivorsNose.Description: You gain an edge on tests made using the Survival skill.

DirtyFighting.Name: Dirty Fighting
DirtyFighting.Description: At the end of each of your turns, each enemy adjacent to you takes [[/damage @M]]{damage} equal to your Physique score.

DownTheAlley.Name: Down the Alley
DownTheAlley.Effect_after00000000000: The target can’t be hidden from you for 24 hours. Until the end of the encounter, whenever the target willingly moves, you can use a free triggered action to move.

KillerRep.Name: Killer Rep
KillerRep.Story: Your reputation hits before you do, and your opening burst staggers them.
KillerRep.Effect_after00000000000: This ability deals your loadout damage type.

StreetNetwork.Name: Street Network
StreetNetwork.Description: You can talk your way to information from gangers, fixers, and street contacts, and you automatically sense the presence of any such contact within 10 squares of you, even if they’re hidden. When negotiating with a ganger, fixer, or street contact, treat your Renown as 1 higher than usual.

Weathered.Name: Weathered
Weathered.Description: You and each ally within 5 squares of you ignore banes and other negative effects from urban and industrial hazards — toxic fumes, structural collapse, crossfire, and similar. Once per respite, you can call in a favor from a street contact to gain the benefit of a skill of your choice from the exploration group for one scene.

AmbushRush.Name: Ambush Rush
AmbushRush.Story: You strike at the target like the ultimate predator you are.
AmbushRush.Effect_after00000000000: You can shift up to 4 squares, bringing the target with you. While grabbed this way, the target takes [[/damage 2*@M]]{damage} equal to twice your Physique score at the start of each of your turns .

Crossfire.Name: Crossfire
Crossfire.Story: You set up interlocking fields of fire and a grav-lift field for your crew.
Crossfire.Effect_after00000000000:
Until the end of the encounter or until you are dying, each enemy target takes damage of your loadout damage type equal to [[/damage 2*@M type=cold/fire/corruption/lightning]]{twice your Physique score} at the end of each of your turns.

Additionally, you can [[/apply t7CYKliC6xtRG9gk]] (fly, using the grav-lift field) while the aura is active. Each ally target who starts or ends their turn in the area can also [[/apply t7CYKliC6xtRG9gk]] until the start of their next turn or until the effect ends.

Special: When you use this ability outside of combat without spending Adrenaline, you must spend 1 uninterrupted minute setting up the field, and you take [[/damage 1d6]] damage before the ability takes effect. The field lasts for 1 hour or until a combat encounter begins.

GhostOfTheGutter.Name: Ghost of the Gutter
GhostOfTheGutter.Description: You can use any Kit. During a respite, you can swap your Kit and still take another respite activity. Street Network’s sense range extends to 1 mile. Whenever you make a test to track another creature, roll three dice and choose which two to use.

LastWord.Name: Last Word
LastWord.Story: You unleash an otherworldly cry that rips through your enemies, killing the weakest of them.

SaturationFire.Name: Saturation Fire
SaturationFire.Story: You empty everything you’re carrying into the kill zone.
SaturationFire.Effect_after00000000000: This ability deals your loadout damage type and ignores damage immunity.

GrowingAdrenalineStreetVet.Name: Growing Adrenaline
GrowingAdrenalineStreetVet.Description:
You gain certain benefits in combat based on the amount of Adrenaline you have. These benefits last until the end of your turn, even if a benefit would become unavailable to you because of the amount of Adrenaline you spend during your turn. Some Growing Adrenaline benefits can be applied only if you are a specific level or higher, with the level of those benefits noted in the various Growing Adrenaline tables in this section.

Adrenaline

Benefit

2

Whenever you use the Knockback maneuver, the forced movement distance gains a bonus equal to [[lookup @A]]{your Reflex score}.

4

The first time you slide a creature on a turn, you [[/surge 1]].

6

You gain an edge on Reflex tests and the Knockback maneuver

8 (4th Level)

The first time you slide a creature on a turn, you [[/surge 2]].

10 (7th Level)

You have a double edge on Reflex tests and the Knockback maneuver.

12 (10th Level)

Whenever you use a heroic ability, you gain [[/heal 10 temporary]]. Additionally, whenever you make a power roll that imposes forced movement on a target, the forced movement distance gains a bonus equal to [[lookup @A]]{your Reflex score}.

FieldArsenal.Name: Field Arsenal
FieldArsenal.Description:
You carry two Kits. You use the better Stamina, speed, stability, disengage, and melee/ranged distance bonus of the two, and the damage bonus of your preferred Kit.

Set your preferred Kit: on your hero sheet’s Equipment tab, right-click a Kit and choose Make Preferred Kit. A star marks it. Switch it whenever you swap weapons.

Each Kit still needs its own qualifying gear (see the Kits chapter ownership rule).

LoadoutCryo.Name: Loadout: Cryo
LoadoutCryo.Description:
Liquid-nitrogen rounds, freeze grenades, and cryo-lines that lock joints solid. Your loadout damage type is cold.

At 4th level, when you gain Combat Form, enable its cold immunity effect on your sheet (and Warzone Incarnate’s Street-vet cold effect at 10th level).

LoadoutToxin.Name: Loadout: Toxin
LoadoutToxin.Description:
Nerve-agent darts, bio-hazard slugs, and corrosive payloads from the black clinics. Your loadout damage type is corruption.

At 4th level, when you gain Combat Form, enable its corruption immunity effect on your sheet (and Warzone Incarnate’s Street-vet corruption effect at 10th level).

LoadoutIncendiary.Name: Loadout: Incendiary
LoadoutIncendiary.Description:
Dragon’s-breath shells, thermite charges, and phosphorus tracers. Your loadout damage type is fire.

At 4th level, when you gain Combat Form, enable its fire immunity effect on your sheet (and Warzone Incarnate’s Street-vet fire effect at 10th level).

LoadoutShock.Name: Loadout: Shock
LoadoutShock.Description:
Taser rounds, arc-grenades, and capacitor-charged knuckles. Your loadout damage type is lightning.

At 4th level, when you gain Combat Form, enable its lightning immunity effect on your sheet (and Warzone Incarnate’s Street-vet lightning effect at 10th level).

GaspingInPain.Name: Breathless Hit
GaspingInPain.Story: Your precise strikes let your crew take advantage of a target’s agony.
GaspingInPain.Effect_after00000000000: One ally within 5 squares of the target [[/surge 1]].

IWorkBetterAlone.Name: I Work Better Alone
IWorkBetterAlone.Story: “It’s better, just you and me. Isn’t it?”
IWorkBetterAlone.Effect_after00000000000: If the target has none of your allies adjacent to them, you [[/surge 1]] before making the power roll.

TeamworkHasItsPlace.Name: Teamwork Has Its Place
TeamworkHasItsPlace.Story: You hit an enemy the moment a crewmate exposes their weakness.
TeamworkHasItsPlace.Effect_after00000000000: If any ally is adjacent to the target, you [[/surge 1]] before making the power roll.

YouWereWatchingTheWrongOne.Name: You Were Watching the Wrong One
YouWereWatchingTheWrongOne.Story: They can’t watch both of you at once.
YouWereWatchingTheWrongOne.Effect_after00000000000: As long as you have one or more allies within 5 squares of the target, you [[/surge 1]]. If you are flanking the target when you use this ability, choose one ally who is flanking with you. That ally also [[/surge 1]].

DisorientingStrike.Name: Vertigo Burst
DisorientingStrike.Story: Your hit leaves them reeling, and you follow them into the gap.
DisorientingStrike.Effect_after00000000000: You can shift into any square the target leaves when you slide them.

Eviscerate.Name: Eviscerate
Eviscerate.Story: You leave your mark bleeding out after one devastating cut.

GetInGetOut.Name: Get In Get Out
GetInGetOut.Story: Move unexpectedly, strike fast, and be gone.
GetInGetOut.Effect_after00000000000: You can shift up to your speed, dividing that movement before or after your strike as desired.

CoupDeGrace.Name: Kill Confirm
CoupDeGrace.Story: Your blade — or your round — might be the last thing they see.

OneHundredThroats.Name: One Hundred Throats
OneHundredThroats.Story: As you cross the floor, every enemy within reach feels it.
OneHundredThroats.Effect_before0000000000: You shift up to your speed and make one power roll that targets up to three enemies who came adjacent to you during the move.

Neurospike.Name: Neurospike
Neurospike.Story: Your wired-reflex implant dumps a quarter-second of overclock into your nervous system — two strikes inside one heartbeat.
Neurospike.Effect_before0000000000: You use a strike signature ability twice.

Dancer.Name: Dancer
Dancer.Story: You drop into a flow state that makes you nearly impossible to pin down.
Dancer.Effect_before0000000000: Until the end of the encounter, whenever an enemy moves or is force moved adjacent to you or damages you, you can take the Disengage move action as a free triggered action.

MisdirectingStrike.Name: Misdirecting Strike
MisdirectingStrike.Effect_after00000000000: The target is taunted by a willing ally within 5 squares of you until the end of the target’s next turn.

PinningShot.Name: Pinning Shot
PinningShot.Story: One round — placed well and placed hard.

FlashScreen.Name: Flash-Screen
FlashScreen.Story: A wrist-emitter pulse floods the area with broad-spectrum flash — dazzled sensors, thermal-white, saturated HUDs.
FlashScreen.Effect_before0000000000: A flash-emitter screen fills the area until the end of your next turn, granting you and your allies concealment against enemies. While you are in the area, whenever an enemy ends their turn in the area, you can use a free triggered action to shift to a new location within the area and make a free strike against them.

BlindsideShift.Name: Blindside Shift
BlindsideShift.Story: A wired-reflex snatch-and-drag behind the nearest column, into a maintenance duct, or over a railing — and a Ghost Suite emitter pulse on the way back.
BlindsideShift.Effect_before0000000000: You and the target are removed from the encounter map until the start of your next turn. You reappear in the spaces you left or the nearest unoccupied spaces. Make the power roll upon your return; its damage is a thermal-optic pulse.

RooftopRush.Name: Rooftop Rush
RooftopRush.Story: A mag-grip parkour vault and an optical stutter. You vanish. They fall. You reappear.
RooftopRush.Effect_after00000000000: You disappear before making the power roll. After the power roll is resolved, you appear in the first unoccupied space at the far end of the line.

YouTalkTooMuch.Name: You Talk Too Much
YouTalkTooMuch.Story: Silence is a virtue. A round through the larynx — or a jammed commlink — is the next best thing.
YouTalkTooMuch.Effect_after00000000000: The target can’t communicate with anyone until the end of the encounter. [[/apply QcDNVWsfPwbqgWbU]]

Assassinate.Name: Assassinate
Assassinate.Story: A practiced kill on an already weakened mark.
Assassinate.Effect_after00000000000: A target who is not a minion, leader, or solo creature and who is winded after taking this damage is reduced to 0 Stamina.

KillZoneMesh.Name: Kill-Zone Mesh
KillZoneMesh.Story: A throwable micro-emitter mesh snaps open — low-yield thermal lasers on tripwire paint a kill zone.

OverclockCascade.Name: Overclock Cascade
OverclockCascade.Story: Your wired-reflex chrome runs at redline for one second, and the room is already over.
OverclockCascade.Effect_before0000000000: You can use a strike signature ability four times, use a strike signature ability that gains an edge three times, or use a strike signature ability that has a double edge twice. You can shift up to 2 squares between each use.

TheyAlwaysLineUp.Name: They Always Line Up
TheyAlwaysLineUp.Story: One round, fast enough to pass through a line of enemies and hamstring every one of them.

HesitationIsWeakness.Name: Beat the Draw
HesitationIsWeakness.Story: You read a crewmate’s cue and step into the seam.
HesitationIsWeakness.Trigger: Another hero ends their turn. That hero can’t have used this ability to start their turn.
HesitationIsWeakness.Effect_before0000000000: You take your turn after the triggering hero.

CarefulObservation.Name: Glass the Block
CarefulObservation.Story: A moment of focus leaves a foe firmly in your sights.
CarefulObservation.Effect_before0000000000: As long as you remain within distance of the target, maintain line of effect to them, and strike no other creature first, you gain an edge on the next strike you make against the assessed creature, and [[/surge 1]] you can use only on that strike.

NightWatchStrike.Name: Night Watch
NightWatchStrike.Story: A silenced round from nowhere knocks another weapon off course.
NightWatchStrike.Trigger: The target takes damage from another creature’s ability while you are hidden.
NightWatchStrike.Effect_before0000000000: The target takes half the damage. You remain hidden.

Advantage.Name: Advantage
Advantage.Description:
Advantage is the read — the fraction of a second in which an enemy has committed to a bad decision, cashed into precision. You are a fully mundane class: no Veil, no Signal, no magic. Chrome never generates Advantage directly.

Advantage in Combat

At the start of a combat encounter or some other stressful situation tracked in combat rounds (as determined by the Director), you gain Advantage equal to [[lookup @hero.victories]]{your Victories}. At the start of each of your turns during combat, you [[/gain 1d3 hr]]{gain 1d3 Advantage}.

Additionally, the first time each combat round that you deal damage incorporating 1 or more surges, you [[/gain 1 hr]]{gain 1 Advantage}.

Whenever you use a heroic ability that makes use of a power roll, that ability costs 1 fewer Advantage if you have an edge or double edge on it. If the ability has multiple targets, the cost is reduced even if the ability gains an edge or has a double edge against only one target.

You lose any remaining Advantage at the end of the encounter.

Advantage Outside of Combat

Although you can’t gain Advantage outside of combat, you can use your heroic abilities and effects that cost Advantage without spending it. Whenever you use an ability or effect outside of combat that costs Advantage, you can’t use that same ability or effect outside of combat again until you earn 1 or more Victories or finish a respite.

When you use an ability outside of combat that lets you spend unlimited Advantage on its effect, such as the Ghost subclass’s Grapnel-Blink, you can use it as if you had spent an amount of Advantage equal to [[lookup @hero.victories]]{your Victories}.

Surges

A surge is a stored, one-shot damage boost — the read paying off on the trigger pull, the cut, or the placed shot. Several Scout abilities and features give you surges. You spend a surge by adding damage to a strike: +2 damage at Echelon 1, +3 at Echelon 2, +4 at Echelon 3, +5 at Echelon 4. A single strike can use multiple surges, and they stack. Unspent surges are lost at the end of the encounter.

In Foundry, Advantage costs are enforced in combat at the ability’s full cost: you can’t use a heroic ability with less Advantage than it costs. Apply the edge discount by adjusting the spend in the use dialog.

KeepItDown.Name: Keep It Down
KeepItDown.Description: While conversing with any creature you share a language with, you can decide whether anyone else can perceive what you’re conveying, even while yelling (throat-modulator and laryngeal-focus chrome).

NightWatch.Name: Night Watch
NightWatch.Description:
Your sense for stealth shows those around you how to evade notice. While you are hidden, enemies take a bane on tests made to search for you or other hidden creatures within 10 squares of you.

Additionally, you have the Night Watch triggered ability.

SurgeOfAdvantage.Name: Surge of Advantage
SurgeOfAdvantage.Description: The first time each combat round that you deal damage incorporating 1 or more surges, you gain 2 Advantage instead of 1.

GhostSuite.Name: Ghost Suite
GhostSuite.Description:
Your prototype optical-camo and dermal chromatic-camo array is class-granted chrome: it doesn’t use a chrome slot or Body Integrity.

As a maneuver, you activate the suite. You stay in Ghost Suite mode until the end of the encounter, until you are dying, or until you deactivate it after 1 uninterrupted hour of quiet focus outside of combat. While it’s active, you gain the following effects: [[/apply GS0000000000suit]]

  • You can automatically climb at full speed while moving (mag-grip gauntlets and boots).

  • Enemies’ spaces don’t count as difficult terrain for you. An enemy takes thermal-optic damage equal to [[lookup @A]]{your Reflex score} the first time you pass through their space on a turn. [[/damage @A]]

  • If you end your turn with cover or concealment from another creature, you are automatically hidden from that creature.

  • You [[/surge 1]] at the start of each of your turns.

  • You have thermal-optic damage immunity equal to 5 + your level.

  • The suite’s emitters run hot: creatures gain an edge on strikes against you.

  • You take a bane on Persona tests made to interact with other creatures.

SharperEye.Name: Sharper Eye
SharperEye.Description: At the start of each of your turns during combat, you [[/gain 1d3+1 hr]]{gain 1d3 + 1 Advantage} instead of 1d3.

CarefulObservationImprovementI.Name: Glass the Block Improvement I
CarefulObservationImprovementI.Description: You can target two creatures simultaneously with your Glass the Block ability, observing both. Making a strike against one target doesn’t end your observation of the other target.

Ventriloquist.Name: Ventriloquist
Ventriloquist.Description: Whenever you communicate, you can throw your voice so that it seems to originate from a creature or object within 10 squares (the same laryngeal-modulator chrome the Mask Rig fields at higher fidelity). If you are hidden, talking this way doesn’t cause you to be revealed.

GhostSquad.Name: Ghost Squad
GhostSquad.Description:
Your Ghost Suite paints persistent, moving optical-camo decoys of you, backed by your crew’s shared HUD feed. At the start of each of your turns, you can forgo gaining Advantage to create [[/roll 1d6]] chromatic decoys of yourself in unoccupied adjacent spaces. A decoy acts on your turn and uses your statistics, except they have 1 Stamina. They are affected by any conditions and effects on you, and last until the start of your next turn. A decoy doesn’t have Advantage and can’t use the Careful Observation ability, the Ghost Suite feature, or any triggered actions. On their turn, a decoy has a move action, a maneuver, and a main action that they can use only to make a free strike. While making a free strike, a decoy must choose targets that you or another decoy aren’t also striking.

Outside of combat, you can have one decoy active for every 2 Victories you have. If a decoy is destroyed, you must wait 1 hour before creating another one.

DeathPool.Name: Death Pool
DeathPool.Description: The first time each combat round that you deal damage incorporating 1 or more surges, you gain 3 Advantage instead of 2.

CarefulObservationImprovementII.Name: Glass the Block Improvement II
CarefulObservationImprovementII.Description: You can target three creatures simultaneously with your Glass the Block ability.

GhostSuiteImproved.Name: Ghost Suite Improved
GhostSuiteImproved.Description:
You gain full control over your Ghost Suite, and you can end it at will (no action required). The suite now runs cold: while it’s active you are always wreathed in optical distortion that grants you concealment, and creatures no longer gain an edge on strikes against you.

Once per day, while your Ghost Suite is active, you can spend 1 uninterrupted minute concentrating on a location where you’ve previously placed a Ghost Suite navigation beacon. At the end of that minute, you and each willing creature of your choice within 10 squares of you are extracted to unoccupied spaces of your choice within that location (a pre-scouted grapnel and mag-cable route through a vertical shaft or ductwork). Each creature who travels this way is invisible for 1 hour or until they use an ability.

Subterfuge.Name: Subterfuge
Subterfuge.Description:
You have an epic resource called Subterfuge. Each time you finish a respite, you gain Subterfuge equal to the XP you gain. You can spend Subterfuge on your abilities as if it were Advantage.

Additionally, you can spend Subterfuge to take additional maneuvers on your turn. You can use one maneuver for each Subterfuge you spend.

Subterfuge remains until you spend it.

Quarry.Name: Hard Tag
Quarry.Story: You mark the target the way an old-line hunter marks a deer, and the mark stays.
