SmitersZeal.Description: Your smiting workings (Judgment’s Hammer, Curse of Terror, Corruption’s Curse, Vessel of Retribution) increase in magnitude by one step: +2 damage on each result, or +1 to any forced movement (Director’s call per ability).

BladeOfTheChosen.Name: Blade of the Chosen
BladeOfTheChosen.Description: You gain the benefit of Consecrated Weapon / Damned Weapon now instead of at 9th level: your weapon strikes deal extra holy (Light) or corruption (Dark) damage equal to [[lookup @P]]{your Persona score}. At 9th level you gain no additional benefit from that feature.

DoubleJudgment.Name: Twin Judgment
DoubleJudgment.Description: Judgment can hold a second target at the same time. The Conviction gain triggers only once per round across both marks.

ZealousStrike.Name: Zealous Strike
ZealousStrike.Description: Smite / Rebuke deals 1 extra damage per result step (+1 low, +2 middle, +3 high) against a target under Judgment.

IronFaith.Name: Iron Faith
IronFaith.Description: While you have at least 1 Conviction, your Stamina maximum increases by your level.

WrathfulMomentum.Name: Wrathful Momentum
WrathfulMomentum.Description: Judgment’s Hammer knocks the target prone on any result, including low.

AnathemasWeight.Name: Anathema’s Weight
AnathemasWeight.Description: A target under your Judgment has a bane on saving throws against your ongoing effects.

VengeanceUnbound.Name: Vengeance Unbound
VengeanceUnbound.Description: When the target under your Judgment damages you, your next Smite / Rebuke against it gains an edge.

ConsecratedGround.Name: Consecrated Ground
ConsecratedGround.Description: When you cast Sanctuary Ward, allies inside it also deal +1 damage with melee strikes.

WrathOfTheChosen.Name: Wrath of the Chosen
WrathOfTheChosen.Description: Once per encounter, when you reduce the target under your Judgment to 0 Stamina, you immediately regain Conviction as if an encounter had just started ([[lookup @hero.victories]]{your Victories}), and you can place Judgment on a new target for free.

Exorcist.Name: Exorcist
Exorcist.Description:
“Containment / counter-thaumic specialist.” The Veil specialist: banishment, warding against incursion, and sensing and dispelling corruption and possession, with the edge against spirits, the corrupted, and dark entities. Your Invoke the Pact entity is a hunting or binding spirit.

At 1st level you gain the Occult skill, the Discerning Eye feature, and an Exorcist ability of your choice.

DiscerningEye.Name: Discerning Eye
DiscerningEye.Description: Your Sense the Veil / Discern Spirits is enhanced: on a high (17+) result you also learn a hostile spirit’s true name (setting up an edge on a later banishment), and your reads always tell willingly bound entities from coerced or hostile ones.

BoundToSilence.Name: Bound to Silence
BoundToSilence.Description: When you banish or dispel a hostile spirit or corrupted target, you can add a save-ends rider: the target is silenced, restrained, or unable to manifest (Director’s choice matching the fiction).

HuntersFocus.Name: Hunter’s Focus
HuntersFocus.Description: Your anti-spirit workings gain an edge against spirits, undead, and corrupted creatures.

ChainOfNames.Name: Chain of Names
ChainOfNames.Description: Invoke the Pact costs 2 less Conviction (minimum 5) when you use it to bind or banish a hostile spirit rather than summon an ally.

SilencingSeal.Name: Silencing Seal
SilencingSeal.Description: Bound to Silence’s rider can also suppress a hostile working (a curse, a possession, an active summon) for its duration, not just the entity itself.

WardAgainstIncursion.Name: Ward Against Incursion
WardAgainstIncursion.Description: A hostile spirit that tries to manifest in or cross into your Sanctuary Ward takes corruption damage equal to [[lookup @P]]{your Persona score}.

MarkedForBanishment.Name: Marked for Banishment
MarkedForBanishment.Description: Once per round, when you hit a spirit or corrupted creature with Smite / Rebuke, you mark it: your next hit against it gains an edge.

PurgingRite.Name: Purging Rite
PurgingRite.Description: Corruption’s Curse cast on a corrupted or possessed creature also removes 1 stack of corruption or possession from it (a cleanse rather than a curse, at the Director’s fiction call).

HuntersBind.Name: Hunter’s Bind
HuntersBind.Description: Your hunting spirit (Invoke the Pact, extension form) gains an edge on rolls made to track or restrain a spirit.

SeveringWord.Name: Severing Word
SeveringWord.Description: Fear of the Gods cast against a spirit or corrupted target also ends one of its ongoing summon or bind effects.

UnbrokenCircle.Name: Unbroken Circle
UnbrokenCircle.Description: The first round each encounter that you sustain Sanctuary Ward against an active spirit incursion, it drains no Conviction.

TheLastRite.Name: The Last Rite
TheLastRite.Description: Once per encounter, as a free action, spend any amount of Conviction (minimum 5) to attempt an immediate banishment of a spirit or corrupted creature within range, whatever its rank.

Class.Name: Hacker
Class.Description:
You are a Hacker — a ghost in the machine who fights wars in the Wired before the first physical shot is fired. Your cyberdeck is your weapon, Bandwidth is your fuel, and Programs are your spells. Outside combat you are the crew’s key to any door, camera, lock, drone, or vault with a wire running to it; inside combat you are a second front the enemy usually can’t see coming.

The Wired: every hero has the nine Matrix Verbs (Connect, Jack Out, Toggle Connection State, Scan, Navigate, Ping, Broadcast, Search, Read/Write) and the Overlay / Jacked In connection states. Your Hacking skill gives you an edge on every rolled Matrix Verb, and Jacked In adds an edge on Wired power rolls. Programs that require you or an ally to be “Jacked In or Overlaid” read those same statuses.

Your kit is a cyberdeck, not a weapon. Your subclass is your Hacking Doctrine: Disruptor (striker), Controller (the sysop), or Support (guardian angel in the net).

You are chrome-positive: Wired implants (Sub-Dermal Radio, Encephalon, Simsense Booster, Signal Ghost) make you better, and Cyborgs make superb Hackers.

Core characteristics: Logic, Instinct · Heroic resource: Bandwidth · Starting Stamina: 19 (+7 per level) · Recoveries: 9 · Kit: cyberdeck. Quick Build: Disruptor, Nyx Cartel “Switchblade”.

Bandwidth.Name: Bandwidth
Bandwidth.Description:
Bandwidth is the Hacker’s fuel for Programs.

Bandwidth in Combat

  • Start of combat: gain Bandwidth equal to [[lookup @hero.victories]]{your Victories}.

  • Income: at the start of each of your turns, gain [[/gain 1 hr]]{1 Bandwidth} (automatic in Foundry), plus your cyberdeck’s Bandwidth Bonus (Switchblade [[/gain 2 hr]]{+2}, Padlock-6 or Lookout [[/gain 1 hr]]{+1}). Bandwidth Overclock (7th level) raises the base income to +2.

  • Natural 19 or 20: whenever you roll a natural 19 or 20 on any power roll, [[/gain 1 hr]]{gain 1 Bandwidth}.

Cap: 6 × your echelon (8 × echelon with Bandwidth Overclock).

Reset: you lose all Bandwidth at the end of the encounter, unless you have Infinite Loop (10th level).

Bandwidth Outside of Combat

You can’t gain Bandwidth outside combat, but you can use Bandwidth-costing Programs without spending it. Once you do, you can’t use that same Program outside combat again until you earn 1 or more Victories or finish a respite. Programs with their own outside-combat clauses (Seize Control, Deep Scan, Ghost Signal, Backdoor Override) work as their text says.

Trace Alert: a low (≤11) result on a Wired power roll usually raises the target host’s 12-step Trace Alert (tracked on the Wired Console); your deck’s Alert Discount reduces those increases.

In Foundry, the base +1 is automatic; your deck bonus, natural 19/20 gains, and the cap use the buttons above.

ExploitTheBreach.Name: Exploit the Breach
ExploitTheBreach.Description: Whenever your Deep Scan gets a high (17+) result, the target has a marked exploitable weakness until the end of the encounter (or until it’s scanned again). The next Wired hit against it from you or an ally gains an edge, and a Track 2 hit also deals +2 Integrity damage. Only one target can be marked at a time.

ImprovedCyberdeck.Name: Improved Cyberdeck
ImprovedCyberdeck.Description: You gain +1 to your Intrusion Roll Modifier and +1 Integrity Damage Bonus at every result band, on top of your equipped deck. This comes from the class, not the deck, so it persists if you swap decks.

BandwidthOverclock.Name: Bandwidth Overclock
BandwidthOverclock.Description: Your base Bandwidth income increases from +1 to +2 per turn ([[/gain 1 hr]]{add the extra 1}), and your Bandwidth cap increases from 6 × echelon to 8 × echelon.

RootAccess.Name: Root Access
RootAccess.Description: You can use Dual Boot twice per encounter. Improved Cyberdeck’s bonus becomes +2 to your Intrusion Roll Modifier and +2 Integrity Damage Bonus at every result band (replacing the +1).

InfiniteLoop.Name: Infinite Loop
InfiniteLoop.Description:
Your Bandwidth no longer fully resets between encounters: you keep Bandwidth equal to your echelon (4 at 10th level) instead of dropping to 0. The first 2 points of Bandwidth over your cap in a round are kept for one round instead of lost.

In Foundry, Draw Steel sets your Bandwidth to your Victories when combat starts; add your retained Bandwidth with a button. [[/gain 4 hr]]{Gain 4 retained Bandwidth}

GhostSignal.Name: Ghost Signal
GhostSignal.Effect_before0000000000:
Distance: Reach.

No roll. The target is untraceable and unlisted on the Wired until the end of the encounter, or until they take a hostile Wired action themselves.

Outside combat: scrub a commlink signature from local logs and cameras for a scene.

KillSwitch.Name: Kill Switch
KillSwitch.Story: Cut the target’s legs out from under it.
KillSwitch.Tier2: Integrity damage equal to your deck’s middle-band Integrity Damage Bonus; the target loses its maneuver on its next turn.
KillSwitch.Tier3: Integrity damage equal to your deck’s middle-band bonus; the target loses its main action on its next turn.

FailsafeCascade.Name: Failsafe Cascade
FailsafeCascade.Story: The net catches you before the fall.
FailsafeCascade.Effect_before0000000000:
Distance: Reach.

No roll. The target regains Stamina equal to twice your deck’s Biofeedback Resistance, and is shielded from the next instance of Integrity-to-Stamina biofeedback bleed-through this encounter.

NetworkPurge.Name: Network Purge
NetworkPurge.Tier2: Each target takes Integrity damage equal to your deck’s middle-band bonus.
NetworkPurge.Tier3: Each target takes Integrity damage equal to your deck’s middle-band bonus and has a bane on its next power roll.

BackdoorOverride.Name: Backdoor Override
BackdoorOverride.Effect_before0000000000:
Distance: Reach.

No roll, by design.

  • Track 1 object: an automatic high (17+) breach.

  • Track 2 target: Integrity damage equal to your deck’s middle-band bonus, with no Trace Alert increase.

Outside combat: an automatic clean breach of any lock, vault, or system, with no roll and no Alert cost.

SeizeControl.Name: Seize Control
SeizeControl.Story: Breach it and use it, in the same breath.
SeizeControl.Effect_before0000000000:
Distance: Reach.

One activation breaches the target’s security and lets you use it this turn. This is your primary out-of-combat lever: doors, lights, and power matter even with no ICE present. Add your deck’s Intrusion Roll Modifier.
SeizeControl.Tier1: Brief, one-shot control; Trace Alert increases.
SeizeControl.Tier3: Solid, lasting control, and choose one: refund the maneuver, or leave no trace.

DeepScan.Name: Deep Scan
DeepScan.Effect_before0000000000:
Distance: Reach.

Free, but still a real power roll. Passive observation doesn’t raise Trace Alert. Sets up a follow-up Seize Control.
DeepScan.Tier2: The specific make and model of one or two Wired items on the target.
DeepScan.Tier3: A full readout of everything Wired-connected on the target, and a marked exploitable weakness (Exploit the Breach).

GhostStep.Name: Ghost Step
GhostStep.Trigger: A Track 2 target (ICE, a hostile AI Persona, a rival decker) targets you directly, or the Trace Alert increases from your own action.
GhostStep.Effect_before0000000000: No Bandwidth cost. Choose one: immediately use a maneuver-cost Matrix Verb for free, or cancel the Trace Alert increase entirely (once per encounter).

DualBoot.Name: Dual Boot
DualBoot.Trigger: You make a Program, Matrix Verb, or signature power roll.
DualBoot.Effect_before0000000000: Once per encounter (twice with Root Access), apply a second deck you own’s Intrusion Roll Modifier and Integrity Damage Bonus to this roll instead of your equipped deck’s, whichever is better. Bandwidth Bonus, Alert Discount, Biofeedback Resistance, Reach, and Ghost Distance don’t change.

GhostProtocol.Name: Ghost Protocol
GhostProtocol.Trigger: An encounter begins, after you had at least one uninterrupted round of Overlay or Jacked In access before initiative (Director’s call).
GhostProtocol.Effect_before0000000000: You and your allies gain an edge on your first power roll of the encounter, and you can use one free Matrix Verb or Deep Scan before the first turn begins.

GhostInTheMachine.Name: Ghost in the Machine
GhostInTheMachine.Effect_before0000000000: Once per encounter, treat the roll as a natural 19 if the actual result was lower: a low or middle result becomes a guaranteed high (17+), and it also triggers the natural 19/20 bonus Bandwidth ([[/gain 1 hr]]).

BorrowedAccess.Name: Borrowed Access
BorrowedAccess.Story: Lend your deck to a crewmate.
BorrowedAccess.Effect_before0000000000:
Distance: Reach.

The ally immediately uses one Program you know that costs 5 Bandwidth or less, using your deck’s stats and your Bandwidth, without spending their own action.

Disruptor.Name: Disruptor
Disruptor.Description:
Striker, damage amplification. Hard, fast, single-target intrusion strikes that punish Track 2 targets and amplify the whole crew’s damage against ICE, hostile deckers, and AI Personas.

At 1st level you gain Overclocked Damage and the Cascade Strike triggered action. Quick Build deck: Nyx Cartel “Switchblade”.

OverclockedDamage.Name: Overclocked Damage
OverclockedDamage.Description: Your own successful Track 2 hits deal +1 Integrity damage.

CascadeStrike.Name: Cascade Strike
CascadeStrike.Trigger: Any Track 2 target takes Integrity damage from anyone.
CascadeStrike.Effect_before0000000000:
Distance: Reach.

Add +2 Integrity damage to that hit.

OverclockedStrikes.Name: Overclocked Strikes
OverclockedStrikes.Description: Overclocked Damage’s bonus on your own hits increases from +1 to +2. (Cascade Strike’s bonus on others’ hits stays +2.)

CascadeFailure.Name: Cascade Failure
CascadeFailure.Story: One host goes down and takes another with it.
CascadeFailure.Trigger: You reduce a Track 2 target to 0 Integrity.
CascadeFailure.Effect_before0000000000:
Distance: Reach.

Another Track 2 target within Reach immediately takes Integrity damage equal to your deck’s low-band Integrity Damage Bonus.

NoSecondChances.Name: No Second Chances
NoSecondChances.Description: Cascade Strike can also apply Exploit the Breach’s marked-weakness edge to the same hit, even if you didn’t scan the target.

OverwhelmIce.Name: Overwhelm ICE
OverwhelmIce.Tier1: Integrity damage equal to half your deck’s low-band bonus (round down); Trace Alert increases.
OverwhelmIce.Tier2: Integrity damage equal to your deck’s middle-band bonus, plus Overclocked Damage.
OverwhelmIce.Tier3: Integrity damage equal to your deck’s high-band bonus, plus Overclocked Damage, and the target has a bane on its next roll.

HairTrigger.Name: Hair Trigger
HairTrigger.Description: You can use Cascade Strike twice per round (still 1 Bandwidth each).

TotalBreach.Name: Total Breach
TotalBreach.Description: Overclocked Damage’s bonus on your own hits increases to +3, and whenever you reduce a Track 2 target to 0 Integrity, you [[/gain 2 hr]]{regain 2 Bandwidth}.

ZeroDay.Name: Zero Day
ZeroDay.Effect_before0000000000:
Distance: Reach.

The roll has an edge. Whatever the result, the target takes Integrity damage equal to your deck’s high-band bonus, plus Overclocked Damage (a low result still raises Trace Alert).
ZeroDay.Tier3: The target also can’t act on its next turn.

Controller.Name: Controller
Controller.Description:
“The Sysop.” Lockdown, node control and holding. A specialist in seizing and holding fixed systems, turning nodes into weapons and tripwires against anyone who tries to take them back.

At 1st level you gain Extra Node and the Lockout triggered action. Quick Build deck: Ferrum “Padlock-6”.

ExtraNode.Name: Extra Node
ExtraNode.Description: You can hold 1 more node than your deck’s normal limit.

Lockout.Name: Lockout
Lockout.Trigger: An enemy attempts to retake or break your hold on a node you seized.

RedundantSystems.Name: Redundant Systems
RedundantSystems.Trigger: You lose control of a node you hold.
RedundantSystems.Effect_before0000000000:
Distance: Reach.

Once per encounter, attempt to re-seize the node with no maneuver or main action cost.
RedundantSystems.Tier1: You fail to re-seize it; Trace Alert increases.
RedundantSystems.Tier3: You re-seize the node, and it counts as freshly seized.

Chokepoint.Name: Chokepoint
Chokepoint.Effect_before0000000000: No roll. Until your next turn, any Track 2 target that breaches, retakes, or routes through a node you hold takes a bane and alerts you immediately, even if you aren’t Jacked In.

WiderNet.Name: Wider Net
WiderNet.Description: Extra Node’s bonus increases from 1 to 2 extra held nodes.

PuppetStrings.Name: Puppet Strings
PuppetStrings.Effect_before0000000000:
Distance: Reach.

No roll. Use the held node’s normal function once (a turret, camera, drone, or smartlink) without counting against its own action economy.

IronGrip.Name: Iron Grip
IronGrip.Description: Lockout imposes a double bane instead of a bane.

TotalAwareness.Name: Total Awareness
TotalAwareness.Description: You always know when a node you hold is targeted for a retake, breach, or disruption, even off-map or out of Reach, and you can spend a maneuver to act on it as though it were in Reach.

MasterSysop.Name: Master Sysop
MasterSysop.Tier1: Seize 1 of them (your choice); Trace Alert increases.
MasterSysop.Tier3: Seize all 3; none count against your held-node limit for the rest of the encounter.

Support.Name: Support
Support.Description:
“Guardian angel in the net.” Tank, anchor, ally protection. Your value extends to the whole crew: feeding allies edges and softening Wired-side blows before they reach flesh.

At 1st level you gain Wired Guard and the Dampen triggered action. Quick Build deck: Meridian “Lookout”.

WiredGuard.Name: Wired Guard
WiredGuard.Description: Allies within your Reach who are Jacked In or Overlaid gain a +1 defense bonus against Track 2 attacks.

Dampen.Name: Dampen
Dampen.Story: Soften the blow before it reaches flesh.
Dampen.Trigger: A nearby Jacked In ally takes a hit from a Track 2 target.

WatchfulRelay.Name: Watchful Relay
WatchfulRelay.Description: Wired Guard’s defense bonus increases from +1 to +2.

SignalBoost.Name: Signal Boost
SignalBoost.Story: A clean feed for a crewmate.
SignalBoost.Effect_before0000000000:
Distance: Reach.

No roll. The target gains an edge on their next power roll (Wired or physical) before your next turn.

StandingWatch.Name: Standing Watch
StandingWatch.Description: Dampen can trigger off a Track 2 hit against any ally within Reach, not just Jacked In or Overlaid allies. The reduction stays 2.

EmergencyPatchHacker.Name: Emergency Patch
EmergencyPatchHacker.Story: Patch the crewmate, not just the connection.
EmergencyPatchHacker.Effect_before0000000000:
Distance: Reach.

No roll. The target regains Stamina equal to 2 + your echelon. If the target is Jacked In, this also cancels the next biofeedback bleed-through against them this encounter.

AnchorPoint.Name: Anchor Point
AnchorPoint.Description: Wired Guard’s defense bonus increases to +3, and allies within Reach who are Jacked In also gain your deck’s Biofeedback Resistance as bonus resistance of their own.

FullCoverage.Name: Full Coverage
FullCoverage.Description: The first Dampen you use each round costs 0 Bandwidth; additional uses still cost 1.

GuardianAngelInTheNet.Name: Guardian Angel in the Net
GuardianAngelInTheNet.Effect_before0000000000:
Distance: Reach.

No roll. Until your next turn, each target gains double your Wired Guard defense bonus (+6 at 7th level and later) against Track 2 attacks, and biofeedback bleed-through against them is reduced by an additional 3.

Class.Name: Technomancer
Class.Description:
Closest to a Talent with an Elementalist's conjured-presence trigger and one Conduit signature; Cyborgs cannot take this class.

You are a Technomancer — a shaman, ghost-talker, the one who speaks to the net. You reach into the Wired with your mind alone, and what answers are sprites: fragments of living code that swarm to your will. A Data-sprite scouts, an Attack-sprite bites, a Machine-sprite mends, a Ward-sprite shields. Sprites are conjured Resonance — free, temporary, immaterial, and gone when the current fades — not the Wrench’s bought-and-built drones.

Your techno-magic fills a niche no one else can: Resonance Mending heals machines, drones, vehicles, chrome, and Cyborgs.

⚠ Cyborgs can never be Technomancers. Arcane Severance blocks all magic, including Resonance. You can heal a Cyborg; a Cyborg can’t become you. The hero sheet refuses the combination.

Light chrome tolerance: you sit between the chrome-positive Hacker and Wrench and the chrome-averse Veil casters. Each point of Body Integrity spent on chrome beyond a free allowance of 2 gives a cumulative −1 to Resonance-based power rolls (at most −3).

Your subclass is your discipline: Sprite-Weaver (go wide), Machine-Whisperer (the Cyborg-mending specialist), or Resonance-Warrior (offense at higher risk).

Core characteristics: Logic, Persona · Heroic resource: Resonance · Starting Stamina: 18 (+8 per level) · Recoveries: 8 · Kit: light, optional. Quick Build: Sprite-Weaver, No Kit.

Resonance.Name: Resonance
Resonance.Description:
Resonance is your live bond with the Wired’s spirit world, deepening as your congregation of sprites grows and works.

Earning Resonance

  • Attunement: the first time each encounter you commune with the Wired (compile a sprite or take a Resonance action), gain Resonance equal to [[lookup @hero.victories]]{your Victories}.

  • The congregation: at the start of each of your turns, gain 1 Resonance for each sprite currently compiled under your command (up to your sprite cap). Foundry adds [[/gain 1 hr]]{1} automatically; add the rest.

  • Compile momentum: when you compile a new sprite, [[/gain 1 hr]]{gain 1 Resonance} (Sprite-Weaver: [[/gain 2 hr]]{+2}).

  • Harmonic echo: the first time each round one of your sprites lands an effect (an attack connects, a heal lands, a Wired verb succeeds), [[/gain 1 hr]]{gain 1 Resonance}.

You lose all Resonance at the end of the encounter, and sprites still compiled then decompile (unless a feature says otherwise).

Outside of Combat

You can use a Resonance ability without spending Resonance in a social or exploration scene. You can’t use that same ability outside combat again until you earn a Victory or finish a respite.

Firewall: Resonance is never bought or fed by nuyen or Body Integrity; chrome and foci can make abilities better but never generate Resonance.

In Foundry, Draw Steel sets Resonance to your Victories when combat starts and adds 1 each turn; the per-sprite drip, momentum, and echo use the buttons above.

SpriteCongregation.Name: Sprite Congregation
SpriteCongregation.Description:
Sprites are conjured code-spirits: compiled from Resonance, acting under your command, and decompiling when dismissed (a free maneuver), destroyed (0 Stamina), or at the end of the encounter.

Sprite cap: 2 at 1st level (Sprite-Weaver 3). The baseline rises to 3 at 5th level and 4 at 8th level. Caps never stack — use the highest single number you qualify for. Compile cost: 3 Resonance for an extra sprite beyond Compile Sprite’s free one (Sprite-Weaver 2).

Archetypes

  • Data-sprite (scout and screen): an edge on Search, Scan, breach, or command rolls made by you or an ally directing it; allies gain an edge on power rolls against a target it scanned this round.

  • Attack-sprite (damage): strikes Wired targets directly, or flesh through a device or jack, for [[/damage 2d10+@R]]{2d10 + Logic} damage.

  • Machine-sprite (mender): repairs machines, drones, vehicles, and chrome, and channels Resonance Mending onto Cyborgs.

  • Ward-sprite (shield): a bane on Wired and EW attacks against you (and nearby allies at higher ranks); resists ICE and EW on your behalf.

Sprite Stats

ArchetypeMinor (L1–3)Intermediate (L4–7)Advanced (L8–10)
DataStamina 8 + Logic × level; edge on 1 roll typeStamina 14 + Logic × level; 2 roll typesStamina 20 + Logic × level; all Wired rolls it can see
AttackStamina 12 + Logic × level; 2d10 + LogicStamina 18 + Logic × level; 2d10 + Logic + 1d6Stamina 26 + Logic × level; 3d10 + Logic
MachineStamina 10 + Logic × level; mends 1 Recovery-worthStamina 16 + Logic × level; +1 targetStamina 22 + Logic × level; a full Resonance Mending
WardStamina 10 + Logic × level; bane on attacks against itStamina 16 + Logic × level; bane, self + 1 adjacent allyStamina 22 + Logic × level; double bane, self + all adjacent allies

Draw Steel has no defense scores: attacks against a sprite are ordinary power rolls.

Hybrid bands

  • Minor (1st–3rd level) — extension: sprites act on your turn as extensions of you. No separate initiative.

  • Intermediate (4th–7th) — commanded: sprites act on their own turn, but only if you issue a command (Compile Sprite as a maneuver) each round.

  • Advanced (8th–10th) — independent: sprites take their own turn in the round and act like a proper summon.

Sprites acting on your own turn never trigger biofeedback for you.

Sprite actors are in Ghostwire Summons & Machines › Sprites (one per archetype and hybrid band); set Stamina to the live formula when you place one.

Biofeedback.Name: Biofeedback
Biofeedback.Description:
Overreach bites back, but gently. Only abilities where you spend 5 or more Resonance trigger a biofeedback risk: make a Physique test at the difficulty its cost sets (test difficulties as Draw Steel Heroes prints them).

Resonance spentBiofeedback test
5easy
7medium
9hard
11hard, with a bane

Sprite-Weavers roll every biofeedback test with an edge; Resonance-Warriors with a bane. On a success, nothing happens. On a failure, you take [[/damage @P]]{damage equal to your Persona score} that bypasses temporary Stamina, and the ability still resolves.

Never lethal: if biofeedback would drop you to 0 Stamina, you are Winded instead of dying, and you regain 1 Stamina per turn until stabilized. Only external damage can kill you.

WiredNative.Name: Wired Native
WiredNative.Description: You are a full citizen of the Wired: you use nodes, Trace Alert, and the Matrix Verbs exactly as the Hacker and Wrench do, with no deck or rig. Your body is the interface.

CongregationSense.Name: Congregation Sense
CongregationSense.Description: You always know the current Stamina, position, and sprite rank of every sprite you command within Wired range, even through walls.

CyborgMending.Name: Cyborg Mending
CyborgMending.Description: Resonance Mending’s Cyborg branch is yours from 1st level, whatever your discipline: a Cyborg you mend spends one of their own Recoveries at no Resonance cost, and you can bring a Cyborg at 0 Stamina back to minimal function. This is the class’s headline niche and is never discipline-gated.

LightChromeTolerance.Name: Chrome Erosion
LightChromeTolerance.Description:
Chrome erodes your Resonance cap by the shared chrome magic-erosion formula: −1 per 2 Integrity spent on Standard chrome (round down), per 3 on Soft, per 1 on Salvage. No caster is exempt. A resonance-tuned focus item (a totem, jury-rigged antenna, or string of compiled charms) grants an edge on Resonance-based power rolls and is not chrome, so it causes no erosion.

Arcane Severance: Cyborgs can never take Technomancer levels. A Technomancer who becomes a Cyborg loses all access to Resonance, sprites, and this class’s abilities unless the conversion is reversed.

SpriteCap3.Name: Sprite Cap 3
SpriteCap3.Description: Your baseline sprite cap rises to 3 (if it isn’t already higher).

SpriteCap4.Name: Sprite Cap 4
SpriteCap4.Description: Your baseline sprite cap rises to 4 (if it isn’t already higher).

MasterOfTheCurrent.Name: Master of the Current
MasterOfTheCurrent.Description: Your capstone. Once per encounter, you can use any one heroic ability you know without spending Resonance, and that use never triggers a biofeedback save. The first time you use this each session, your sprite cap is also unlimited for the rest of the encounter (compiles beyond the free use still cost Resonance).

CompileSprite.Name: Compile Sprite
CompileSprite.Effect_before0000000000:
Distance: Wired range.

Compile (main action): a sprite of your choice (Data, Attack, Machine, or Ward) manifests under your control, if you are under your sprite cap. Command (maneuver): your compiled sprites move and act (on your turn, per the extension model).
CompileSprite.Effect_spend00000000000: Compile a second sprite in the same action (Sprite-Weaver: 2 Resonance), or command your whole congregation at once.
CompileSprite.Tier1: The sprite manifests unstable (it acts next turn instead of now), or a command garbles (Director’s call).
CompileSprite.Tier2: The sprite compiles, or the command resolves, normally.
CompileSprite.Tier3: You compile a sprite and issue a free command in the same action.

ResonanceStrike.Name: Resonance Strike
ResonanceStrike.Effect_before0000000000:
Distance: Wired range, or a sprite’s reach.

You, or a commanded Attack-sprite, lash one enemy with hostile code: a Wired target directly, or a flesh target through a device it carries or a sprite jacked into it.

Your Resonance skill grants an edge on Resonance tests — a power roll never adds a skill. Resonance-Warrior: Overcharged Strike raises this ability’s damage to 3d10 + Logic.
ResonanceStrike.Effect_spend00000000000: A second sprite strikes too, or the roll gains an edge through deep communion.
ResonanceStrike.Tier1: The strike fails to connect, so it deals no damage, and the current recoils (a minor biofeedback risk if you enhanced this past 5 Resonance).
ResonanceStrike.Tier3: Plus a rider: a Wired condition (glitched — a bane on the target’s next power roll, or blinded sensors) or a free sprite reposition.

ResonanceMending.Name: Resonance Mending
ResonanceMending.Story: The only healing in the game that puts a Cyborg back together.
ResonanceMending.Effect_before0000000000:
Distance: Touch, or Wired range for a jacked or networked target (Machine-Whisperer: Wired range always).

Base effect (free): the target regains Stamina or Integrity equal to one Recovery’s worth. A Cyborg target instead spends one of their own Recoveries at no Resonance cost. Every Technomancer can mend a Cyborg from 1st level. No roll is needed unless you mend against resistance (a hostile EW field or contested Wired space) as an enhanced main action.
ResonanceMending.Effect_spend00000000000: For each Resonance spent, choose one (repeatable): reach one additional target; clear one save-ends mechanical condition (a jam, glitch, suppression, or chrome malfunction); grant one additional Recovery spend. For 2 Resonance, restore a dead machine, failed chrome, or a Cyborg at 0 Stamina to minimal function (1 Stamina or Integrity). Spending 5 or more on one use triggers biofeedback.
ResonanceMending.Tier1: Contested: the mend is unstable; after one round the target loses half of what was restored unless stabilized.
ResonanceMending.Tier2: Contested: the mend lands as purchased.
ResonanceMending.Tier3: Contested: the mend lands, and the target also clears one minor condition.

Recompile.Name: Recompile
Recompile.Story: Always the right ghost to hand.
Recompile.Effect_before0000000000:
Distance: Wired range.

Reshape a compiled sprite into another archetype (Data → Attack, Attack → Ward, and so on), or instantly recompile a sprite destroyed this round at reduced power (half Sprite HP).

HarmonicAdjustment.Name: Harmonic Adjustment
HarmonicAdjustment.Effect_before0000000000:
Distance: Wired range.

Choose one: the sprite gains an edge on its power roll this turn, a double bane on attacks against it until the end of your next turn, or a free shift up to its full movement.

SwarmTheSignal.Name: Swarm the Signal
SwarmTheSignal.Effect_before0000000000:
Distance: Wired range.

Every sprite you command takes an action at once against a single target or objective: all attack one foe, all mend one machine, or all pile onto one node. (Sprite-Weaver 5th level: split across up to 3 targets.)

DeepCommunion.Name: Deep Communion
DeepCommunion.Effect_before0000000000:
Distance: The Wired, or a machine, drone, or Cyborg you’re attuned to.

You project fully into the Wired (or into an attuned machine, drone, or Cyborg), gaining edges on Wired verbs and sprite commands and using the system’s own reach and senses. Your body goes inert and exposed, as if Jacked In. No control rig needed. (Machine-Whisperer: 2 Resonance.)

ResonanceCascade.Name: Resonance Cascade
ResonanceCascade.Story: A lash of hostile code that fans out.
ResonanceCascade.Tier1: One enemy only, and it is dazed until the end of its next turn.
ResonanceCascade.Tier2: Up to 2 enemies within 3 squares of each other.
ResonanceCascade.Tier3: Up to 3 enemies within distance, each dazed until the end of their next turn.
ResonanceCascade.Effect_before0000000000: A thin lash of hostile code that fans out the harder you focus it. The power roll sets how many enemies within distance it reaches; each one takes the damage shown.

SpriteRedirect.Name: Sprite Redirect
SpriteRedirect.Story: A code-spirit thrown into the path of a bullet.
SpriteRedirect.Trigger: An ally within Wired range or 10 squares is hit by a Wired attack.
SpriteRedirect.Effect_before0000000000: Redirect the attack to one of your compiled sprites; the sprite absorbs the hit in the ally’s place.

ResonanceWard.Name: Resonance Ward
ResonanceWard.Effect_before0000000000:
Distance: A zone around you.

Until your next turn, you weave a zone of resonant protection with Ward-sprites and a standing harmonic: Wired and EW attacks against allies in it take a bane, chrome and devices in it are screened from hijack, and you can counter hostile intrusion in the area.

Biofeedback: easy Physique test (Sprite-Weaver rolls with an edge; Resonance-Warrior with a bane). On a failure you take [[/damage @P]]{damage equal to your Persona score} that bypasses temporary Stamina; the ability still resolves. Biofeedback can’t drop you below Winded.

Overclock.Name: Overclock
Overclock.Effect_before0000000000:
Distance: Wired range.

Each compiled sprite acts twice this turn.

Biofeedback: easy Physique test (Sprite-Weaver rolls with an edge; Resonance-Warrior with a bane). On a failure you take [[/damage @P]]{damage equal to your Persona score} that bypasses temporary Stamina; the ability still resolves. Biofeedback can’t drop you below Winded.

TranceCompile.Name: Trance Compile
TranceCompile.Effect_before0000000000:
Distance: Wired range.

Compile two new sprites (any archetypes) in a single action, within your sprite cap. Both act normally after compiling.

Biofeedback: easy Physique test (Sprite-Weaver rolls with an edge; Resonance-Warrior with a bane). On a failure you take [[/damage @P]]{damage equal to your Persona score} that bypasses temporary Stamina; the ability still resolves. Biofeedback can’t drop you below Winded.

SignalWeave.Name: Signal Weave
SignalWeave.Story: Tuning forks laid across the battlefield’s signal.
SignalWeave.Effect_before0000000000:
All allies gain an edge on Wired-based power rolls for the rest of the round, and one enemy of your choice within distance is glitched (a bane on its next power roll).

Biofeedback: easy Physique test (Sprite-Weaver rolls with an edge; Resonance-Warrior with a bane). On a failure you take [[/damage @P]]{damage equal to your Persona score} that bypasses temporary Stamina; the ability still resolves. Biofeedback can’t drop you below Winded.

TotalResonance.Name: Total Resonance
TotalResonance.Effect_before0000000000:
Distance: Wired range.

For the rest of the encounter, every sprite you command rises one rank on the hybrid ladder (minor acts as intermediate; intermediate as advanced), your congregation drip doubles, and you immediately compile one additional sprite for free, ignoring your sprite cap for the rest of the encounter. The rank boost is unconditional; the roll only decides the free sprite.

Biofeedback: medium Physique test (Sprite-Weaver rolls with an edge; Resonance-Warrior with a bane). On a failure you take [[/damage @P]]{damage equal to your Persona score} that bypasses temporary Stamina; the ability still resolves. Biofeedback can’t drop you below Winded.
TotalResonance.Tier1: The free sprite compiles unstable (half Stamina); the rank boost still applies.
TotalResonance.Tier2: The free sprite compiles at full strength but acts next turn.
TotalResonance.Tier3: The free sprite compiles at full strength and acts immediately.

CascadeFailureTechno.Name: Cascade Failure
CascadeFailureTechno.Story: One roll, and the whole cube shorts out.
CascadeFailureTechno.Effect_before0000000000:
One power roll shorts out the whole cube. Each enemy the roll reaches takes the damage shown.

Biofeedback: medium Physique test (Sprite-Weaver rolls with an edge; Resonance-Warrior with a bane). On a failure you take [[/damage @P]]{damage equal to your Persona score} that bypasses temporary Stamina; the ability still resolves. Biofeedback can’t drop you below Winded.
CascadeFailureTechno.Tier1: Only the nearest enemy is affected, and it is stunned (save ends).
CascadeFailureTechno.Tier2: Up to 2 enemies of your choice, each stunned until the end of their next turn.
CascadeFailureTechno.Tier3: Up to 4 enemies of your choice, each stunned (save ends), and their next Wired ability fizzles.

SpriteStorm.Name: Sprite Storm
SpriteStorm.Effect_before0000000000:
Compile 3 sprites in a single action (Sprite-Weaver: 4). All your compiled sprites strike different targets within 10 squares as part of the same action.

Biofeedback: medium Physique test (Sprite-Weaver rolls with an edge; Resonance-Warrior with a bane). On a failure you take [[/damage @P]]{damage equal to your Persona score} that bypasses temporary Stamina; the ability still resolves. Biofeedback can’t drop you below Winded.

ResonanceSlam.Name: Resonance Slam
ResonanceSlam.Story: The current hits like a wall.
ResonanceSlam.Effect_before0000000000:
Choose one mode. Slam: one target takes [[/damage 3*@R]]{damage equal to three times your Logic score}, is pushed 3 squares, and is weakened (save ends). Slam Group: each enemy in a 3 cube within 5 squares takes [[/damage @R]]{damage equal to your Logic score} and is knocked prone.

Biofeedback: medium Physique test (Sprite-Weaver rolls with an edge; Resonance-Warrior with a bane). On a failure you take [[/damage @P]]{damage equal to your Persona score} that bypasses temporary Stamina; the ability still resolves. Biofeedback can’t drop you below Winded.

TheChoirSingsTogether.Name: The Choir Sings Together
TheChoirSingsTogether.Story: A resonant chord that steels the crew.
TheChoirSingsTogether.Effect_before0000000000:
Each target gains [[/heal 2*@P temp]]{temporary Stamina equal to twice your Persona score}, and a Machine-sprite channels a mending pulse: each target can spend a Recovery.

Biofeedback: hard Physique test (Sprite-Weaver rolls with an edge; Resonance-Warrior with a bane). On a failure you take [[/damage @P]]{damage equal to your Persona score} that bypasses temporary Stamina; the ability still resolves. Biofeedback can’t drop you below Winded.

RewireReality.Name: Rewire Reality
RewireReality.Story: Hijack a mind or machine into your congregation.
RewireReality.Effect_before0000000000:
If the target has Persona < STRONG, then for the rest of the encounter it counts as one of your compiled sprites: it still acts on its own initiative, but you can Command it as a maneuver. Otherwise it takes [[/damage 2*@R]]{damage equal to twice your Logic score} instead.

Biofeedback: hard Physique test (Sprite-Weaver rolls with an edge; Resonance-Warrior with a bane). On a failure you take [[/damage @P]]{damage equal to your Persona score} that bypasses temporary Stamina; the ability still resolves. Biofeedback can’t drop you below Winded.

WiredSilence.Name: Wired Silence
WiredSilence.Effect_before0000000000:
For the next round, no Wired-based attack (Hacker, Wrench, Technomancer, device, or drone) functions in the area. Hostile sprites in the area decompile; friendly sprites lose one rank for the round.

Biofeedback: hard Physique test (Sprite-Weaver rolls with an edge; Resonance-Warrior with a bane). On a failure you take [[/damage @P]]{damage equal to your Persona score} that bypasses temporary Stamina; the ability still resolves. Biofeedback can’t drop you below Winded.

BoneDeepCommunion.Name: Bone Deep Communion
BoneDeepCommunion.Effect_before0000000000:
For the rest of the encounter, your sprites count as one rank higher (an advanced sprite is already at the top of the ladder, so it instead gains +6 Stamina, or +8 for an Attack-sprite) and your Resonance drip gains +1 per turn.

Biofeedback: hard Physique test on cast and at the start of each later round (Sprite-Weaver rolls with an edge; Resonance-Warrior with a bane). On a failure, take [[/damage @P]]{damage equal to your Persona score}; you can’t drop below Winded.

SunlightInTheWire.Name: Sunlight in the Wire
SunlightInTheWire.Story: The net answers with full illumination.
SunlightInTheWire.Effect_before0000000000:
Enemy sprites within distance decompile. Allied sprites in the area act at the highest rank for the rest of the encounter. Each ally in the area can spend a Recovery and gains temporary Stamina equal to a minor sprite’s Stamina (10 + Logic × level).

Biofeedback: hard Physique test with a bane; on a failure, take [[/damage 3*@P]]{damage equal to three times your Persona score} (can’t drop you below Winded).

MachineGodsRite.Name: Machine God’s Rite
MachineGodsRite.Effect_before0000000000:
An in-scene ritual of at least 5 minutes. Restore the target to full Stamina or Integrity. You can’t use this on the same target again for 24 in-game hours.

Biofeedback: hard Physique test with a bane (Sprite-Weaver rolls with an edge; Resonance-Warrior with a double bane). On a failure you take [[/damage @P]]{damage equal to your Persona score} that bypasses temporary Stamina; the ability still resolves. Biofeedback can’t drop you below Winded.

RecompileReality.Name: Recompile Reality
RecompileReality.Effect_before0000000000:
Distance: The past scene.

An in-scene ritual of at least 10 minutes, once per session. Undo one significant Wired event from the past scene (a lockdown, a destroyed drone, a hit to a Cyborg’s chrome): force a reroll, or treat it as though it never happened.

Biofeedback: hard Physique test with a bane; on a failure, take [[/damage 3*@P]]{damage equal to three times your Persona score} and lose one Recovery (can’t drop you below Winded).

TheWeaversWeb.Name: The Weaver’s Web
TheWeaversWeb.Effect_before0000000000:
Compile 5 sprites in a single action; all 5 strike different targets within distance. Each target struck that has Physique < STRONG takes [[/damage 3*@R]]{damage equal to three times your Logic score} and is weakened (save ends).

Biofeedback: hard Physique test with a bane (Sprite-Weaver rolls with an edge; Resonance-Warrior with a double bane). On a failure you take [[/damage @P]]{damage equal to your Persona score} that bypasses temporary Stamina; the ability still resolves. Biofeedback can’t drop you below Winded.

SpriteWeaver.Name: Sprite-Weaver
SpriteWeaver.Description:
Wide congregation. More sprites, cheaper sprites, and a bigger board presence than any other discipline. You roll every biofeedback test with an edge: your power lives in quantity and coordination, not any single risky cast.

At 1st level you gain the Summoning skill and Wide Compile.

WideCompile.Name: Wide Compile
WideCompile.Description: Your sprite cap rises to 3. Compiling an extra sprite costs 2 Resonance instead of 3, and compile momentum grants [[/gain 2 hr]]{+2 Resonance} per new sprite instead of +1.

OverlappingSignals.Name: Overlapping Signals
OverlappingSignals.Description: When Compile Sprite gets a high (17+) result, you can compile a second sprite for free as part of the same action (instead of, not in addition to, its enhancement).

CongregationsChorus.Name: Congregation’s Chorus
CongregationsChorus.Description: Once per round, when two or more of your sprites act on the same turn, each of their rolls gains an edge.

TheWideningGyre.Name: The Widening Gyre
TheWideningGyre.Description: Your sprite cap rises to 4. Swarm the Signal can split the swarm across up to 3 targets.

LegionOfTheCurrent.Name: Legion of the Current
LegionOfTheCurrent.Description: Your sprite cap rises to 5. Once per encounter, you can use Compile Sprite as a free action.

UnbrokenCongregation.Name: Unbroken Congregation
UnbrokenCongregation.Description: Your capstone. Once per session, one sprite doesn’t decompile at the end of an encounter and carries into the next scene (it can still be destroyed). Your sprite cap rises to 6.

MachineWhisperer.Name: Machine-Whisperer
MachineWhisperer.Description:
Interface and healer. The discipline that makes the class’s Cyborg-mending niche its whole identity: the best answer in the game to a downed Cyborg, a wrecked drone, or failing chrome. Biofeedback at the class baseline.

At 1st level you gain the Repair skill and Deep Interface.

DeepInterface.Name: Deep Interface
DeepInterface.Description: Deep Communion costs 2 Resonance instead of 3, and your Physique saves against biofeedback while in communion gain an edge. Resonance Mending reaches Wired range even for its free base effect.

MachineEmpathy.Name: Machine Empathy
MachineEmpathy.Description: Resonance Mending’s enhancements cost 1 less Resonance (minimum 1): restoring a dead machine, chrome, or Cyborg costs 1 instead of 2.

WhisperedDiagnostics.Name: Whispered Diagnostics
WhisperedDiagnostics.Description: Once per round as a free action, inspect one machine, drone, vehicle, or Cyborg within Wired range: learn its exact Stamina or Integrity, its active conditions, and one exploitable weakness.

BondedRepair.Name: Bonded Repair
BondedRepair.Description: Once per encounter, use Resonance Mending’s enhanced effect as if you had spent 3 Resonance, at no Resonance cost and with no biofeedback.

TheMachineRemembers.Name: The Machine Remembers
TheMachineRemembers.Description: When Resonance Mending restores a dead machine, drone, chrome, or Cyborg, it returns at half its Stamina or Integrity instead of 1, and clears one additional condition.

WhisperersCommunion.Name: Whisperer’s Communion
WhisperersCommunion.Description: Your capstone. One Resonance Mending can target any number of machines, drones, and Cyborgs within Wired range: the base effect applies to all of them, and enhancements still apply individually.

ResonanceWarrior.Name: Resonance-Warrior
ResonanceWarrior.Description:
Offensive mystic. The congregation as a weapon, with the highest biofeedback risk for the highest damage ceiling. You roll every biofeedback test with a bane.

At 1st level you gain the Security Systems skill (electronic warfare) and Overcharged Strike.

OverchargedStrike.Name: Overcharged Strike
OverchargedStrike.Description: Resonance Strike deals [[/damage 3d10+@R]]{3d10 + Logic} instead of 2d10 + Logic, and Attack-sprites you command deal an extra [[/damage 1d6]]{1d6} on a hit.

AggressiveCompile.Name: Aggressive Compile
AggressiveCompile.Description: When you compile an Attack-sprite, it can act immediately, even on a low (unstable) compile result.

FeedbackWeapon.Name: Feedback Weapon
FeedbackWeapon.Description: Once per round, when you take biofeedback damage from your own ability, you can deal the same amount of psychic damage to one enemy within 5 squares.

BurningTheCurrent.Name: Burning the Current
BurningTheCurrent.Description: Once per turn, you can voluntarily make a 5-cost biofeedback test (an easy Physique test, with your discipline’s edge or bane) on an ability that wouldn’t normally trigger one, to add your Logic score to that ability’s damage.

NoSuchThingAsTooMuch.Name: No Such Thing As Too Much
NoSuchThingAsTooMuch.Description: Cascade Failure and Resonance Slam are made with an edge, and their damage increases by [[/damage 1d6]]{1d6}.

ApexCurrent.Name: Apex Current
ApexCurrent.Description: Your capstone. Once per encounter, treat a failed biofeedback save as a success. The Resonance spent isn’t refunded.

UndercityBarrens.Name: Undercity Barrens
UndercityBarrens.Description:
You grew up below the city’s foundations — flooded transit tunnels, collapsed arcades, and squatter blocks the corps wrote off decades ago. Down there you learned who runs each tunnel and how to move without being noticed.

Skills: you gain Stealth, and choose one of Streetwise, Survival, Perception, or Athletics. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Your community: you know the Undercity’s squatter blocks, tunnel gangs, and scavenger crews. You have an edge on tests to recall lore about that community or to find and influence people within it (Director’s call on when it applies).

CorpArcology.Name: Corp Arcology
CorpArcology.Description:
You were raised inside a megacorp arcology — company school, company clinic, company everything. You know how departments really work and how to talk your way up a chain of command.

Skills: you gain Corporate, and choose one of Persuasion, Negotiation, Insight, or Security Systems. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Your community: you know your arcology’s departments, company families, and internal security. You have an edge on tests to recall lore about that community or to find and influence people within it (Director’s call on when it applies).

SprawlDistrict.Name: Sprawl District
SprawlDistrict.Description:
You came up in the endless mid-city Sprawl, where every block has its own fixer, its own gang tax, and its own price for everything. You learned to haggle before you learned to read.

Skills: you gain Streetwise, and choose one of Negotiation, Contacts, Perception, or Brawl. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Your community: you know your district’s street vendors, fixers, block associations, and local gangs. You have an edge on tests to recall lore about that community or to find and influence people within it (Director’s call on when it applies).

TransitHub.Name: Transit Hub / Freeport
TransitHub.Description:
You grew up where everything moves: a maglev terminus, a cargo freeport, or an orbital elevator’s base. Everyone passes through, everyone owes someone, and you know every route in and out.

Skills: you gain Navigation, and choose one of Contacts, Driving, Piloting, or Negotiation. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Your community: you know dockworkers, freight crews, customs brokers, and travelers passing through your hub. You have an edge on tests to recall lore about that community or to find and influence people within it (Director’s call on when it applies).

OutlandWastes.Name: Outland Wastes
OutlandWastes.Description:
You’re from beyond the city walls — dead farmland, toxic scrub, and nomad convoys between ruined towns. You’re hard to kill and you know how to keep going when the water runs out.

Skills: you gain Survival, and choose one of Athletics, Driving, Perception, or Firearms. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Your community: you know Outland nomad clans, convoy runners, and wasteland settlements. You have an edge on tests to recall lore about that community or to find and influence people within it (Director’s call on when it applies).

AcademicSpire.Name: Academic Spire
AcademicSpire.Description:
You were raised among a university or research spire’s archives and restricted stacks, where old histories and older forbidden texts sit side by side. You learned what the official record leaves out.

Skills: you gain History, and choose one of Occult, Matrix Theory, Medicine Lore, or Xenology. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Your community: you know your spire’s faculty, archivists, research departments, and rival scholars. You have an edge on tests to recall lore about that community or to find and influence people within it (Director’s call on when it applies).

FaithDistrict.Name: Faith District
FaithDistrict.Description:
You grew up in the shadow of a cathedral of the Light — shelters, soup lines, confessionals, and street preachers. You learned the dogma, and you learned to read the desperate people who came looking for it.

Skills: you gain Religion, and choose one of Insight, Occult, Warding, or Medicine. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Your community: you know the district’s churches, shelters, orders of the Light, and the faithful who depend on them. You have an edge on tests to recall lore about that community or to find and influence people within it (Director’s call on when it applies).

IndustrialDeep.Name: Industrial Deep
IndustrialDeep.Description:
You come from the foundries, mines, and reactor levels under the city — Corran labor towns most often, but open to anyone who grew up on shift work. You can keep any machine running with scrap and stubbornness.

Skills: you gain Engineering, and choose one of Repair, Athletics, Demolitions, or Electronics. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Your community: you know foundry crews, labor unions, and Industrial Deep shift towns. You have an edge on tests to recall lore about that community or to find and influence people within it (Director’s call on when it applies).

WageSlave.Name: Wage-Slave
WageSlave.Description:
You worked a corporate desk job — cubicle hives, quarterly targets, and contracts you weren’t allowed to read. You know the system from the bottom and how to bargain your way through it.

Skills: you gain Negotiation, and choose two of Corporate, Persuasion, Insight, or Electronics. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Starting resources: no Renown or ¥ from the Profession itself. A Director may grant a small ¥ bonus (for example ¥500) as liquid cash — never as skills, perks, or other character-power budget.

StreetDoc.Name: Street Doc
StreetDoc.Description:
You patched up people who couldn’t go to a real clinic: gunshot wounds, back-alley chrome, and overdoses, no questions asked. You learned to read a patient who’s lying about how they got hurt.

Skills: you gain Medicine, and choose two of Cybertech, Insight, Streetwise, or Medicine Lore. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Starting resources: no Renown or ¥ from the Profession itself. A Director may grant a small ¥ bonus (for example ¥500) as liquid cash — never as skills, perks, or other character-power budget.

Fixer.Name: Fixer
Fixer.Description:
You connected people who needed things done with people who could do them, and took your cut. Your commlink is the most valuable thing you own.

Skills: you gain Contacts, and choose two of Negotiation, Streetwise, Insight, or Deception. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Starting resources: no Renown or ¥ from the Profession itself. A Director may grant a small ¥ bonus (for example ¥500) as liquid cash — never as skills, perks, or other character-power budget.

Courier.Name: Courier
Courier.Description:
You moved packages that couldn’t go through the mail — data chips, cash, sometimes things that were still breathing. Fast, quiet, and never late.

Skills: you gain Driving, and choose two of Stealth, Navigation, Athletics, or Streetwise. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Starting resources: no Renown or ¥ from the Profession itself. A Director may grant a small ¥ bonus (for example ¥500) as liquid cash — never as skills, perks, or other character-power budget.

GangSoldier.Name: Gang Soldier
GangSoldier.Description:
You held a corner for a gang: collecting protection money, running off rivals, and shooting when talking stopped working.

Skills: you gain Firearms, and choose two of Intimidation, Streetwise, Brawl, or Melee. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Starting resources: no Renown or ¥ from the Profession itself. A Director may grant a small ¥ bonus (for example ¥500) as liquid cash — never as skills, perks, or other character-power budget.

SecurityGuard.Name: Security Guard
SecurityGuard.Description:
You stood post for a corp, a mall, or a private security contractor. Long hours watching cameras and doorways taught you to spot trouble before it starts.

Skills: you gain Perception, and choose two of Firearms, Intimidation, Security Systems, or Brawl. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Starting resources: no Renown or ¥ from the Profession itself. A Director may grant a small ¥ bonus (for example ¥500) as liquid cash — never as skills, perks, or other character-power budget.

Smuggler.Name: Smuggler
Smuggler.Description:
You moved contraband past checkpoints and scanners — bypassing seals, forging manifests, and knowing which inspector could be paid.

Skills: you gain Security Systems, and choose two of Deception, Contacts, Driving, or Stealth. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

RigTech.Name: Rig-Tech
RigTech.Description:
You maintained and flew drones and remote vehicles for a delivery firm, a security company, or a salvage crew, jacked into the rig.

DeckJockey.Name: Deck Jockey
DeckJockey.Description:
You made a living in the Wired: freelance intrusion work, data brokering, or corp pen-testing. You built your own deck and you know how the network actually thinks.

Entertainer.Name: Entertainer
Entertainer.Description:
You performed for a living — club stages, simstim streams, or street-corner shows. You know how to work a crowd and how to be whoever the audience wants.

BeatReporter.Name: Beat Reporter
BeatReporter.Description:
You chased stories for a newsfeed until one got too close to a corp that didn’t want it told. You notice details, you know how companies hide things, and you have sources everywhere.

Hauler.Name: Hauler / Labor
Hauler.Description:

MercRecruit.Name: Merc Recruit
MercRecruit.Description:
You signed with a private military company or a free company and did a tour in someone else’s war zone. You learned to shoot, march, and survive in the field.

PureHuman.Name: Pure Human
PureHuman.Description:
Baseline humanity — adaptable, balanced, widely compatible. The default point of comparison.

Pure Human Traits

Signature Trait: @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.PBCgnAAsXDXQYBnK]{Detect the Supernatural}

Purchased Pure Human Traits

You have 3 ancestry points to spend on the following traits. (Quick Build: Perseverance, Staying Power.)

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.IKlIxTf6cZBswcDp]{Can’t Take Hold (1 Point)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.BRyUSHVG9fjDwjRo]{Determination (2 Points)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.GLkKrRMeWpCMQD88]{Perseverance (1 Point)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.XltgAaOrbUeRoX36]{Resist the Unnatural (1 Point)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.b7PH3aCTK3kMDiqA]{Staying Power (2 Points)}

PurchasedTraits.Name: Purchased Traits
PurchasedTraits.Description: You have 3 ancestry points to spend on the following traits. (Quick Build: Perseverance, Staying Power.)

CantTakeHold.Name: Can’t Take Hold
CantTakeHold.Description: Your connection to the natural world allows you to resist certain supernatural effects. You ignore temporary difficult terrain created by magic and psionic abilities. Additionally, when you are force moved by a magic or psionic ability, you can reduce the forced movement distance by 1.

Determination.Name: Determination
Determination.Description: A tolerance for pain and distress allows you to push through difficult situations. If you are frightened, slowed, or weakened, you can use a maneuver to immediately end one of those conditions.

Perseverance.Name: Perseverance
Perseverance.Description: Giving up is for other people. You gain an edge on tests made using the Athletics skill when endurance is what’s being tested. Additionally, when you are slowed, your speed is reduced to 3 instead of 2.
Perseverance.EffectDescription: You gain an edge on tests made using the Athletics skill when endurance is what’s being tested. Additionally, when you are slowed, your speed is reduced to 3 instead of 2.

ResistTheUnnatural.Name: Resist the Unnatural
ResistTheUnnatural.Description: Your instinctive resilience protects you from injuries beyond the routine. Whenever you take damage that isn’t untyped, you can use a triggered action to take half the damage.
ResistTheUnnatural.Trigger: You take damage that isn’t untyped

StayingPower.Name: Staying Power
StayingPower.Description: Your human physiology allows you to fight, run, and stay awake longer than others. You increase your number of Recoveries by 2.

DetectTheSupernatural.Name: Detect the Supernatural
DetectTheSupernatural.Description: As a maneuver, you can open your awareness to detect supernatural creatures and phenomena. Until the end of your next turn, you know the location of any supernatural object, or any undead, construct, or creature from another world within 5 squares, even if you don’t have line of effect to that object or creature. You know if you’re detecting an item or a creature, and you know the nature of any creature you detect.

Corran.Name: Corran
Corran.Description:
The engineered underclass — short, sturdy, unbreakable, and done being looked down on.

Corran Traits

Signature Trait: @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.ba1Y2sMZbvtNYExs]{Labor Brand}

Purchased Corran Traits

You have 3 ancestry points to spend on the following traits. (Quick Build: Grounded, Hardened Hide.)

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.habR3HLaizrL2bqS]{Great Fortitude (2 Points)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.QK9VmXg8GMSAihLL]{Grounded (1 Point)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.NkjLgRzuwa9AMGyt]{Hardened Hide (2 Points)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.jiUO0B9qZWmoD300]{Stand Tough (1 Point)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.C5BuTGq5er1JPPcS]{Stone Shaper (1 Point)}

PurchasedTraits.Name: Purchased Traits
PurchasedTraits.Description: You have 3 ancestry points to spend on the following traits. (Quick Build: Grounded, Hardened Hide.)

LaborBrand.Name: Labor Brand
LaborBrand.Description:
You can carve a brand or rune onto your skin with 10 uninterrupted minutes of work, activated by the engineered resilience in your body. The brand you carve determines the benefit, chosen from:

Detection: Pick a specific type of creature (such as Corran or Goliar) or object (such as gems or medkits). Your brand glows softly when you are within 20 squares of any creature or object of that type, even if you don’t have line of effect. You can change the type of creature or object as a maneuver.

Light: Your skin sheds light for 10 squares. You can turn this light on and off as a maneuver.

Voice: As a maneuver, you can communicate telepathically with a willing creature you have met before and who is within 1 mile of you. You must know the creature’s name, and they must speak and understand a language you know. You and the creature can respond as if having a spoken conversation. You can communicate with a different creature by changing the brand.

You can have one brand active at a time, and can change or remove a brand with 10 uninterrupted minutes of work.
LaborBrand.LightEffectDescription: Your skin sheds light for 10 squares. You can turn this light on and off as a maneuver.

GreatFortitude.Name: Great Fortitude
GreatFortitude.Description: Your hearty constitution prevents you from losing strength. You can’t be made weakened.

Grounded.Name: Grounded
Grounded.Description: Your dense frame and connection to the work make it difficult for others to move you. You have a +1 bonus to stability.

HardenedHide.Name: Hardened Hide
HardenedHide.Description: Your engineered skin affords potent protection. You have a +6 bonus to Stamina, and that bonus increases by 6 at 4th, 7th, and 10th levels.

StandTough.Name: Stand Tough
StandTough.Description: Your body is made to withstand the blows of your enemies. Your Physique score is treated as 1 higher for the purpose of resisting potencies, and you gain an edge on Physique tests when called for to resist environmental effects or a creature’s traits or abilities.

StoneShaper.Name: Stone Shaper
StoneShaper.Description: When you spend 1 uninterrupted hour singing or working, you can reshape any unworked mundane stone within 3 squares. You can’t destroy this stone, but you can move each square of it anywhere within 3 squares, piling it off to one side to dig a hole or building it up to create a wall.

Elvani.Name: Elvani
Elvani.Description:
The engineered aristocracy — beautiful, poised, quick, and effortlessly above you.

Elvani Traits

Signature Trait: @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.QjFD2vrzmuFFr47T]{Corp Glamor}

Purchased Elvani Traits

You have 3 ancestry points to spend on the following traits. (Quick Build: High Senses, Otherworldly Grace.)

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.BkApfnE52q6O7XBb]{Glamor of Terror (2 Points)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.CLe3qQ18f2lUheyp]{Graceful Retreat (1 Point)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.pTMx0vJGcnvmQlB0]{High Senses (1 Point)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.ApeGL1aixrw7aRUP]{Otherworldly Grace (2 Points)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.6VKm9YiHiWS0CPER]{Revisit Memory (1 Point)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.H6bwZLNUhvVENjab]{Unstoppable Mind (2 Points)}

PurchasedTraits.Name: Purchased Traits
PurchasedTraits.Description: You have 3 ancestry points to spend on the following traits. (Quick Build: High Senses, Otherworldly Grace.)

CorpGlamor.Name: Corp Glamor
CorpGlamor.Description: A carefully cultivated presence makes others perceive you as interesting and engaging, granting you an edge on Persona tests using the Persuasion skill. This glamor makes you appear and sound slightly different to each creature you meet, since what is engaging to one might be different for another. However, you never appear to be anyone other than yourself.

GlamorOfTerror.Name: Glamor of Terror
GlamorOfTerror.Description: When a foe strikes, you reverse the magic of your glamor to instill fear into their heart. Whenever you take damage from a creature, you can use a triggered action to make that creature frightened of you until the end of their next turn.

GracefulRetreat.Name: Graceful Retreat
GracefulRetreat.Description: You gain a +1 bonus to the distance you can shift when you take the Disengage move action.

HighSenses.Name: High Senses
HighSenses.Description: Your senses are especially keen and perceptive. You gain an edge on tests made to notice threats.

OtherworldlyGrace.Name: Otherworldly Grace
OtherworldlyGrace.Description: Your engineered body and mind can’t be contained for long. Whenever you make a saving throw, you succeed on a roll of 5 or higher.

RevisitMemory.Name: Revisit Memory
RevisitMemory.Description: Accessing memories is as easy as living in the present for you. You gain an edge on tests made to recall lore.

UnstoppableMind.Name: Unstoppable Mind
UnstoppableMind.Description: Your mind allows you to maintain your focus in any situation. You can’t be made dazed.

Goliar.Name: Goliar
Goliar.Description:
The engineered heavy — towering, crushing, and impossible to ignore.

Goliar Traits

Signature Trait: @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.UsFQr3y8rzouYwYc]{Relentless}

Purchased Goliar Traits

You have 3 ancestry points to spend on the following traits. (Quick Build: Glowing Recovery, Grounded.)

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.gGW48sXk6lvWf9ZW]{Bloodfire Rush (1 Point)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.4ouhc5JKDMhvC0U8]{Glowing Recovery (2 Points)}
