Reskinned from the Draw Steel level 2 Rival Talent (Keep). Draw Steel math intact; ability names and rules text rethemed to Ghostwire firearms and chrome (B38c). Placeholder art.

IroncladConscript.Name: Ironclad Conscript
IroncladConscript.Description:
Indentured Ironclad Legion trooper with a bayonet carbine, paying off a debt contract with a body full of company augments and a loyalty collar that explodes if they fall.

Reskinned from the Draw Steel level 1 War Dog Conscript (Keep). Draw Steel math intact; ability names and rules text rethemed to Ghostwire firearms and chrome (B38c). Placeholder art.

IroncladCommando.Name: Ironclad Commando
IroncladCommando.Description:
Ironclad infiltration trooper with suppressed machine pistols, sent in ahead of the line.

Reskinned from the Draw Steel level 1 War Dog Commando (Keep). Draw Steel math intact; ability names and rules text rethemed to Ghostwire firearms and chrome (B38c). Placeholder art.

IroncladSharpshooter.Name: Ironclad Sharpshooter
IroncladSharpshooter.Description:
Ironclad marksman with a spliced targeting eye and a smartgun whose rounds steer around cover.

Reskinned from the Draw Steel level 1 War Dog Sharpshooter (Keep). Draw Steel math intact; ability names and rules text rethemed to Ghostwire firearms and chrome (B38c). Placeholder art.

IroncladSubcommander.Name: Ironclad Subcommander
IroncladSubcommander.Description:
Ironclad squad sergeant with a command sidearm and the kill codes for every collar in the squad.

Reskinned from the Draw Steel level 2 War Dog Subcommander (Keep). Draw Steel math intact; ability names and rules text rethemed to Ghostwire firearms and chrome (B38c). Placeholder art.

IroncladGroundCommander.Name: Ironclad Ground Commander
IroncladGroundCommander.Description:
Ironclad field commander: a company officer who has never lost a contract and doesn’t count the conscripts. Carries a neural tether gun, calls mortar strikes, and holds the master kill code.

Reskinned from the Draw Steel level 3 War Dog Ground Commander (Keep). Draw Steel math intact; ability names and rules text rethemed to Ghostwire firearms and chrome (B38c). Placeholder art.

Zombie.Name: Zombie
Zombie.Description:
A corpse the Veil pushed back up — slow, hungry, and common in the Sinks after a bad night.

Reskinned from the Draw Steel level 1 Zombie (Keep). Stats and abilities are Draw Steel’s; ability text only has faction names updated so far. Placeholder art.

Skeleton.Name: Skeleton
Skeleton.Description:
Veil-risen bones from a flooded Warrens ossuary, still wearing scraps of old uniforms.

Reskinned from the Draw Steel level 1 Skeleton (Keep). Stats and abilities are Draw Steel’s; ability text only has faction names updated so far. Placeholder art.

Ghoul.Name: Ghoul
Ghoul.Description:
Corpse-eater that hunts the Sinks’ body trade.

Reskinned from the Draw Steel level 1 Ghoul (Keep). Stats and abilities are Draw Steel’s; ability text only has faction names updated so far. Placeholder art.

Ghost.Name: Ghost
Ghost.Description:
A Veil ghost anchored to the place it died, often a room the Wired still remembers.

Reskinned from the Draw Steel level 1 Ghost (Keep). Stats and abilities are Draw Steel’s; ability text only has faction names updated so far. Placeholder art.

ChromeRaiderArmiger.Description:
Full-conversion Chrome Raider line-holder: more machine than meat, and proud of it. Flechette carbine, predictive targeting, and a raider beacon that keeps the pack fighting.

Reskinned from the Draw Steel level 3 Time Raider Armiger (Keep). Draw Steel math intact; ability names and rules text rethemed to Ghostwire firearms and chrome (B38c). Placeholder art.

ChromeRaiderHijack.Description:
Chrome Raider ambusher who strips salvage — and chrome — from anything that moves, using forearm monowire lashes and a magnetic grapple harpoon.

Reskinned from the Draw Steel level 3 Time Raider Hijack (Keep). Draw Steel math intact; ability names and rules text rethemed to Ghostwire firearms and chrome (B38c). Placeholder art.

SignalMindkillerWhelp.Description:
A young Signal horror that feeds on minds through a jacked-in connection.

Reskinned from the Draw Steel level 6 Mindkiller Whelp (Keep). Stats and abilities are Draw Steel’s; ability text only has faction names updated so far. Placeholder art.

SignalTalkerInvader.Description:
A Signal Talker that speaks through the Wired and walks through the meat it has hollowed out.

FeralBeast.Name: Feral Beast
FeralBeast.Description:
Feral beast template — a guard dog, a jungle boar, a spire-rat the size of a hound.

Reskinned from the Draw Steel level 1 Animal (Keep). Stats and abilities are Draw Steel’s; ability text only has faction names updated so far. Placeholder art.

VerminSwarm.Description:
A swarm of rats, roaches, or jungle insects boiling out of the walls.

Reskinned from the Draw Steel level 1 Animal Swarm (Keep). Stats and abilities are Draw Steel’s; ability text only has faction names updated so far. Placeholder art.

JungleBeast.Description:

Reskinned from the Draw Steel level 1 Big Animal A (Keep). Stats and abilities are Draw Steel’s; ability text only has faction names updated so far. Placeholder art.

JunglePredator.Description:
Predator template: something big in the jungle that has learned people are easy prey.

Reskinned from the Draw Steel level 1 Predator A (Keep). Stats and abilities are Draw Steel’s; ability text only has faction names updated so far. Placeholder art.

ColorsBoss.Name: Colors Boss
ColorsBoss.Description:
The crew leader who actually gives orders. The gangs of the Flats are named for her colors, not the other way around.

Hook: Drop her and the whole crew’s nerve breaks.

Ghostwire original from The Ossian Reach Handbook, adapted onto the Draw Steel level 1 Goblin Monarch (leader). Draw Steel math; ability names and rules text rethemed to Ghostwire. Placeholder art.
ColorsBoss.Director:
Handbook: Tier 4 Leader (ganger) → Draw Steel level 1 leader, echelon 1.

Colors Up! calls in two Gang Raiders; Focus Fire matches the Handbook Malice move. Run with Gang Raiders or Street Punks. A lower-level alternative to the Gang Boss (level 3).

ChromeBruiser.Name: Chrome Bruiser
ChromeBruiser.Description:
The gang’s cybered heavy: more chrome than credit rating, an auto-shotgun in one hand and a servo-arm for everything else.

Hook: His body integrity is shot — the right EMP payload drops the plating.

Ghostwire original from The Ossian Reach Handbook, adapted onto the Draw Steel level 2 Ogre Goon (elite brute). Draw Steel math; ability names and rules text rethemed to Ghostwire. Placeholder art.
ChromeBruiser.Director:
Handbook: Tier 4 Elite (cyborg brute) → Draw Steel level 2 elite brute, echelon 1.

Handbook traits kept: immune to weakened (Cannot Be Weakened); Warframe Plating is the winded damage immunity. Pair with a Colors Boss.

ResponseLieutenant.Name: ARG Response Lieutenant
ResponseLieutenant.Description:
Argent Exchange’s field commander: a Goliar in ARG hardweave, a smartlinked carbine, a riot-formation squad, and the authority to escalate. ARG Argent Exchange–aligned security.

Hook: He calls the escalation the gazetteer warns about — “Alert response is corporate.”

Ghostwire original from The Ossian Reach Handbook, adapted onto the Draw Steel level 1 Kobold Centurion (leader). Draw Steel math; ability names and rules text rethemed to Ghostwire. Token art: Michael ARG Response Lieutenant / Goliar (B111).
ResponseLieutenant.Director:
Handbook: Tier 4 Leader (corp security) → Draw Steel level 1 leader, echelon 1.

People: Goliar (portrait). Riot Formation only works with allies who share the trait; treat ARG Security Officers fielded with him as having it, or ignore it. Escalate to Lethal is the Handbook villain action; add a drone picket from the vehicles pack for flavor.

CorpNetrunner.Name: Corp Netrunner
CorpNetrunner.Description:
The ICE jockey on overwatch — never leaves the host, rides black ICE down any live connection.

Hook: The reason a Hacker earns their pay. Kill her in meatspace and the whole node goes soft.

Ghostwire original from The Ossian Reach Handbook, adapted onto the Draw Steel level 3 Human Storm Mage (platoon controller). Draw Steel math; ability names and rules text rethemed to Ghostwire. Placeholder art.
CorpNetrunner.Director:
Handbook: Tier 4 Elite (corp hacker) → Draw Steel level 3 platoon controller, echelon 1.

Black ICE Jolt can hit meatspace targets through cyberware and comms, or be run against a jacked-in persona in the Wired. Handbook Trace Master / Lock the Node: advance the Wired Console alert while she is active.

StreetDoc.Name: Street Doc
StreetDoc.Description:
The medic-for-hire who patches anyone with nuyen — no papers, no questions, gunshot wounds treated and never filed.

Hook: A neutral party in most fights, until someone shoots the patient on her table.

Ghostwire original from The Ossian Reach Handbook, adapted onto the Draw Steel level 1 Orc Godcaller (platoon support). Draw Steel math; ability names and rules text rethemed to Ghostwire. Placeholder art.
StreetDoc.Director:
Handbook: Tier 4 Standard (medic specialist) → Draw Steel level 1 platoon support, echelon 1.

Support piece: Adrenal Dart gives allies extra actions and Trauma Patch heals. Often better as a contact than a combatant.

WrenchRigger.Name: Wrench Rigger
WrenchRigger.Description:
The drone handler who owns the pickets over Cassavir’s ground. Fights through drones, not in person.

Hook: The brain behind the flight. Take the Rigger, take the eyes.

Ghostwire original from The Ossian Reach Handbook, adapted onto the Draw Steel level 1 Dwarf Launcher (platoon hexer). Draw Steel math; ability names and rules text rethemed to Ghostwire. Placeholder art.
WrenchRigger.Director:
Handbook: Tier 4 Elite (wrench specialist) → Draw Steel level 1 platoon hexer, echelon 1.

Every attack is delivered by a drone. Place 1–3 drone tokens from the vehicles pack as flavor; the rigger’s own body is soft. Handbook Jumped In (rigger slowed while controlling drones) is optional fiction.

TheWarlord.Name: The Warlord
TheWarlord.Description:
The boss who owns the district. Not the strongest fighter in the Flats — the most entrenched. Trophy shotgun, cyber-fists, and a whole block that answers when he calls.

Hook: Kill him in the open and the district fractures into a turf war by nightfall. Out-plan him; don’t out-punch him.

Ghostwire original from The Ossian Reach Handbook, adapted onto the Draw Steel level 3 Orc Warleader (leader). Draw Steel math; ability names and rules text rethemed to Ghostwire. Placeholder art.
TheWarlord.Director:
Handbook: Tier 3 Solo (ganger boss) → Draw Steel level 3 leader, echelon 1.

Built on a Draw Steel leader spine, not a solo: run him with Gang Raider squads (The Whole Block Answers summons four) and Razorline Prime for the climax fight. No One Leaves is the Handbook villain action.

RazorlinePrime.Name: Razorline Prime
RazorlinePrime.Description:
The augmented duelist — reflex-boosted, a monowire garrote in one hand and a smartgun in the other.

Hook: The Warlord’s personal enforcer and the reason challengers stop coming.

Ghostwire original from The Ossian Reach Handbook, adapted onto the Draw Steel level 2 Bugbear Sneak (elite ambusher). Draw Steel math; ability names and rules text rethemed to Ghostwire. Placeholder art.
RazorlinePrime.Director:
Handbook: Tier 3 Elite (cyborg duelist) → Draw Steel level 2 elite ambusher, echelon 1.

Pure damage and tempo. Ghost-Step stands in for the Handbook reaction. Pair with The Warlord.

ContractEnforcer.Name: Contract Enforcer
ContractEnforcer.Description:
The specialist a corp sends to close the file: full combat chrome, a smartlinked AP carbine, jump-jets, and the whole escalation ladder behind him.

Hook: Killing him flags the crew for the conglomerate’s next tier of response.

Ghostwire original from The Ossian Reach Handbook, adapted onto the Draw Steel level 6 War Dog Tetrarch (leader). Draw Steel math; ability names and rules text rethemed to Ghostwire. Placeholder art.
ContractEnforcer.Director:
Handbook: Tier 3 Leader (cyborg corp security) → Draw Steel level 6 leader, echelon 2.

The Handbook calls this block Corp Enforcer; renamed so it is not confused with the Wave 1 ARG Corporate Enforcer (level 1 squad lead). Bring an ARG Response Lieutenant and ARG Security Officers for Corporate Escalation.

IroncladWarden.Name: Ironclad Warden
IroncladWarden.Description:
The black-site chief of security — an Ironclad trainer promoted to run a site the corp does not admit exists. Shock-shield, riot cannon, bulwark plating.

Hook: He turns a room into a fortress and buys time for the escalation. Flank him or the fight never ends.

Ghostwire original from The Ossian Reach Handbook, adapted onto the Draw Steel level 6 Hobgoblin Grandguard (platoon defender). Draw Steel math; ability names and rules text rethemed to Ghostwire. Placeholder art.
IroncladWarden.Director:
Handbook: Tier 3 Elite (Ironclad defender) → Draw Steel level 6 platoon defender, echelon 2.

Uses the Ironclad Malice features (Fodder Run, Field Salvage, Fire for Effect) — field with Ironclad Conscripts and Commandos.

ChromeRat.Name: Chrome-Rat
ChromeRat.Description:
Corp-lab rodents bred true and hungry in the Warrens: matte-metal teeth and a nose that homes on live wiring.

Hook: The cheapest way to start a session in the dark. If the mission depends on a device, the rats found it first.

Ghostwire original from The Ossian Reach Handbook, adapted onto the Draw Steel level 1 Crawling Claw (minion harrier). Draw Steel math; ability names and rules text rethemed to Ghostwire. Placeholder art.
ChromeRat.Director:
Handbook: Tier 5 Minion / Swarm (beast) → Draw Steel level 1 minion harrier, echelon 1.

Chew the Line is a scene tool: cut lights, doors, or Wired access in a zone.

TunnelBat.Name: Tunnel-Bat
TunnelBat.Description:
Echolocating cave flyers that roost in the Reach’s vertical dead-spaces. Their screaming fritzes cheap AR rigs.

Hook: An alarm with teeth. Wake the roost and every hostile in earshot knows where the crew is.

Ghostwire original from The Ossian Reach Handbook, adapted onto the Draw Steel level 1 Soot Crow (minion harrier). Draw Steel math; ability names and rules text rethemed to Ghostwire. Placeholder art.
TunnelBat.Director:
Handbook: Tier 5 Standard / Swarm (beast) → Draw Steel level 1 minion harrier, echelon 1.

Whiteout Roost punishes ranged fire and deckers near the swarm.

ScrapHound.Name: Scrap-Hound
ScrapHound.Description:
Feral augmented guard dogs gone to ground — jaw-plated, wired for pack coordination, territorial to the death.

Hook: Someone has been feeding them. Find out who, and why they wanted this level guarded.

Ghostwire original from The Ossian Reach Handbook, adapted onto the Draw Steel level 1 Worg (horde mount). Draw Steel math; ability names and rules text rethemed to Ghostwire. Placeholder art.
ScrapHound.Director:
Handbook: Tier 5 Standard (beast brute) → Draw Steel level 1 horde mount, echelon 1.

Run in packs of 3–5; Pack Hunter turns corridors into killboxes.

SinkCrawler.Name: Sink-Crawler
SinkCrawler.Description:
What a blind cave scavenger becomes after generations of drinking the Dark in the Sinks: pallid, wrong-jointed, silent, and far too large.

Hook: The deeper the crew goes, the older and bigger these get. The one that took the last crew is still down there.

Ghostwire original from The Ossian Reach Handbook, adapted onto the Draw Steel level 1 Shieldscale Drangolin (Size 2) (elite brute). Draw Steel math; ability names and rules text rethemed to Ghostwire. Placeholder art.
SinkCrawler.Director:
Handbook: Tier 3 Elite (Veil-touched beast) → Draw Steel level 1 elite brute, echelon 1.

Claws deal corruption damage. Handbook Drag Under: at the Director’s option, a grabbed victim is pulled underground when it burrows. Raise its level for deep Sinks runs.

GutterSerpent.Name: Gutter-Serpent
GutterSerpent.Description:
Long, oil-slick ambush hunters of Slackwater’s overflow channels — part eel, part reptile, a sensor frill breaking the filthy surface.

Hook: The body in the channel wasn’t murdered. Probably.

Ghostwire original from The Ossian Reach Handbook, adapted onto the Draw Steel level 1 Lizardfolk Scaletooth (platoon brute). Draw Steel math; ability names and rules text rethemed to Ghostwire. Placeholder art.
GutterSerpent.Director:
Handbook: Tier 4 Standard (beast) → Draw Steel level 1 platoon brute, echelon 1.

Place in water; Ambush from the Murk gives it a strong opener.

CanopyStalker.Name: Canopy-Stalker
CanopyStalker.Description:
A jungle apex the size of a hovercab beyond Cinderhold’s Outer Wall: fast, feathered, hooked-clawed, hunting in packs from the canopy.

Hook: Longtooth’s caravan didn’t come back. The Rangers found the wagon, and only the wagon.

Ghostwire original from The Ossian Reach Handbook, adapted onto the Draw Steel level 3 Lightbender Pouncer (elite harrier). Draw Steel math; ability names and rules text rethemed to Ghostwire. Placeholder art.
CanopyStalker.Director:
Handbook: Tier 3 Elite (apex beast) → Draw Steel level 3 elite harrier, echelon 1.

Wilds seed only — raptor stand-in until the wilds lore pass. Open from concealment above with Drop from the Green.

ReachBehemoth.Name: Reach Behemoth
ReachBehemoth.Description:
Vehicle-scale primeval megafauna from the deep jungle — the thing the wall was built for. A crushing maw, feeding tendrils, and ground that shakes when it moves.

Hook: Not an encounter to win. Bar the gate, break line of sight, and pray it loses interest before dawn.

Ghostwire original from The Ossian Reach Handbook, adapted onto the Draw Steel level 7 Kingfissure Worm (solo solo). Draw Steel math; ability names and rules text rethemed to Ghostwire. Placeholder art.
ReachBehemoth.Director:
Handbook: Tier 2 Solo (apex megafauna) → Draw Steel level 7 solo solo, echelon 3.

Wilds seed only. Draw Steel solo spine; feeding tendrils are 5 × 1 lines with 35 Stamina each (see Feeding Tendrils) — track them as simple markers.

WatchdogIce.Name: Watchdog ICE
WatchdogIce.Description:
Standard corporate intrusion countermeasure: patrol routines that pace the datascape, sniff for intruders, and raise the alert.

Hook: It already saw the decker. The clock is running.

Ghostwire original from The Ossian Reach Handbook, adapted onto the Draw Steel level 1 War Dog Neuronite (horde defender). Draw Steel math; ability names and rules text rethemed to Ghostwire. Placeholder art.
WatchdogIce.Director:
Handbook: Tier 4 Standard (construct ICE) → Draw Steel level 1 horde defender, echelon 1.

Wired encounter token. Pairs with the Wired Console node templates (docs/directors/wired-node-templates.md): advance the node alert while it is active.

ScramblerIce.Name: Scrambler ICE
ScramblerIce.Description:
Mid-tier disruptive ICE of jagged, strobing geometry that attacks the runner’s own kit rather than tracing them.

Hook: It’s trying to strand the decker in the node long enough for something worse to arrive.

Ghostwire original from The Ossian Reach Handbook, adapted onto the Draw Steel level 3 Time Raider Mind Punk (platoon hexer). Draw Steel math; ability names and rules text rethemed to Ghostwire. Placeholder art.
ScramblerIce.Director:
Handbook: Tier 3 Elite (construct ICE) → Draw Steel level 3 platoon hexer, echelon 1.

Wired encounter token. Handbook Glitch the Kit: at the Director’s option, a target hit by it has one installed program switched off until they spend a main action to reboot it.

BlackIce.Name: Black ICE
BlackIce.Description:
Lethal countermeasure that reaches back down the connection to stop a heart or fry a brain. The Wired’s apex predator.

Hook: Nobody guards nothing with Black ICE. Whatever’s behind this wall is worth a life — is it worth the decker’s?

Ghostwire original from The Ossian Reach Handbook, adapted onto the Draw Steel level 6 Mindkiller (elite hexer). Draw Steel math; ability names and rules text rethemed to Ghostwire. Placeholder art.
BlackIce.Director:
Handbook: Tier 2 Elite (lethal construct ICE) → Draw Steel level 6 elite hexer, echelon 2.

Wired encounter token. Biofeedback Kill: damage it deals to a jacked-in persona carries to the runner’s body.

MamaCassavir.Name: Mama Cassavir, “the Switchboard”
MamaCassavir.Description:
The Reach’s default job-giver: Mama Cassavir, “the Switchboard.” She looks like an elderly wise-woman — a good cosmetician and soft chrome sell the grandmother. Underneath the cosmetics she is a datajacked cyborg, a Controller hacker who sits at the junction of everything that moves through the middle of the hive. She takes clean-branded contracts down from the Spires and corp cut-outs, and dirty ones up from Nyx’s Churn, and connects the crew to whichever end pays. She is not a human tactician and not muscle — she is the phone, the node everyone in the Flats routes through.

Stratum: Upper Flats — a shuttered transit exchange she wired back to life and named herself after.

Hook: Severing her would cut a hundred quiet deals at once, so no one does. She sells introductions, not people; she will burn a client to protect a crew, never the reverse. Cross her once and you don’t get killed — you get disconnected.

Holds: No turf — connections. Every gang in the Flats needs her more than she needs any of them; the Ninth Ward Kings keep their peace with the fixer-world through her.

Answers to / leans on: No one. She leans on reputation, the Wire, and leverage, and keeps a cold, professional back-channel to Cael Marrow at Cinderhold.

Table use: Patron first: the campaign’s on-ramp, the voice that opens most sessions, the safe contact who can hand the crew any hook. A relationship to spend and endanger — an obstacle only if the crew burns her. If it comes to a fight, she is a cyborg Controller with a Wire kit and people, not a Rival Tactician.

Named Ghostwire level-boss from the Lore Source. Draw Steel level 5 elite controller; Cyborg hacker Controller (identity lock 2026-09-20). Token art: Michael split-face portrait (0.3.48) — elderly organic / chrome cyborg, cyan eye, hand on the Switchboard deck.
MamaCassavir.Director:
Named boss — echelon 2.

Cyborg Controller (not a human Rival Tactician). Keywords humanoid, cyborg. Negotiation first (Interest 3, Patience 4; motivations Legacy and Greed; pitfall Authority). She fights with the Wire kit and her people (Make the Call, Seize Control, Everyone Owes Mama, Lockout, Puppet Strings). The holdout is implant-weapon backup only — do not open with it. Surround her with Reach Streets NPCs per The Switchboard. Body Integrity high; soft chrome sells the grandmother look.

WardenKrael.Name: Warden Krael, “the Landlord”
WardenKrael.Description:
A corrupt corp Grid-warden who runs his levels as a private fief. He is the licensed authority, and he sells it: which flats get maintenance, which SIN flags get overlooked, which Metermen corridor operates. The face of the Grid’s rented, corruptible order — a petty tyrant with a corp badge.

Stratum: The Grid — his assigned residential levels.

Hook: Hire him, blackmail him, or replace him. His ledger is the weapon: whoever holds proof of what he has sold owns the Landlord.

Holds: Licensed Grid levels, on paper — residential corridors, lift-stacks, and the Metermen racket that keeps them calm.

Answers to / leans on: A corp facilities-management chain that doesn’t look too hard. Leans on the Metermen, his off-board muscle.

Table use: Both: the crew’s cleanest Grid patron and a ready-made obstacle when a job crosses his fief.

Named Ghostwire level-boss from the Lore Source. Draw Steel level 6 Devil High Judge (leader leader) math; abilities rethemed to Ghostwire. Placeholder art.
WardenKrael.Director:
Named boss — echelon 2.

Draw Steel level 6 leader spine (Devil High Judge): charm effects become badge authority, SIN flags, and pacification emitters; True Name becomes Paper Trail — presenting proof of his corruption strips his defenses. Negotiation: Interest 3, Patience 2; motivations Greed and Power; pitfall Justice. Field ARG Security Officers as his on-duty help; Metermen stay off the board as leverage.

TheFerryman.Name: The Ferryman
TheFerryman.Description:
The level-boss of the descent. Neither gang-lord nor fixer but tollkeeper: he owns the grey-transit chokepoints where the hive stops being watched. Quiet, old, and unbothered by the corps, because he sits where they don’t want to go.

Stratum: The Flats/Sinks boundary — the last controlled crossings down.

Hook: Nothing goes down or comes up without his say. He is the patron for any run that goes deep, and the last friendly face before the dark.

Holds: The down-shafts and the boundary crossings.

Answers to / leans on: No one above. Something below may answer to him.

Table use: Both: patron and gatekeeper for Sinks runs; a chokepoint boss if the crew tries to cross without paying.

Named Ghostwire level-boss from the Lore Source. Draw Steel level 3 Time Raider Tyrannis (leader) math; abilities rethemed to Ghostwire. Placeholder art.
TheFerryman.Director:
Named boss — echelon 1.

Draw Steel level 3 leader spine (Time Raider Tyrannis) rethemed to a dead-air shotgun, shaft-running crew, and a mined grav-locked crossing (Close the Crossing). He walks at speed 5 instead of the Tyrannis’s teleport. Negotiation: Interest 2, Patience 4; motivations Greed and Peace; pitfall Discovery — don’t pry into what lives below. Field Gang Raiders or Street Punks as his crossing crew.

TheChoirmother.Name: The Choirmother
TheChoirmother.Description:
A cult-mother who feeds and protects her people in exchange for devotion, and her charity is real — which is exactly why it’s dangerous. To the players she can read as sincere saint, Concord plant, or already gone thin, because from the outside those look identical.

Stratum: The Flats — a devoted residential block run as a congregation.

Hook: “The Shepherd’s Crook”: a member of her flock, or a hidden-remnant Street Priest who recognizes the Concord’s fingerprints, hires the crew to find out what’s really happening on her block — or to extract someone before they’re “counseled” into the Reliquary Deep.

Holds: A devoted residential block.

Answers to / leans on: She’d say the Light. In truth she leans on a soft-spoken Choir of the Silent Sun “mentor” and the Radiant Concord’s quiet patronage.

Table use: Both: a patron and sanctuary who may be the most tragic obstacle in the Flats. Expose her and a block that depends on her shatters; reach the true Shepherd underneath, or walk away and let the conversion finish.

Named Ghostwire level-boss from the Lore Source. Draw Steel level 3 High Elf Ordinator (leader) math; abilities rethemed to Ghostwire. Placeholder art.
TheChoirmother.Director:
Named boss — echelon 1.

The truth: she is a true daughter of the Light being hollowed out from above by the Radiant Concord, and does not know it.

Director dial — Early / Mid / Late (Fallen): Early (kindled, courted) — still mostly true; the Concord’s hand is a whisper, and a crew that sees it could save her. Mid (hollowing) — this Actor’s default: charity still real, doctrine already drifting; she defends her mentor and files doubters as lapsed. Late / Fallen (counterfeit) — a Concord asset in all but name, Conviction spent, her block a feeder for the Reliquary Deep; she would still pass any sincerity test. For Early, lean on The Light Provides and Rebuke of the Light; for Fallen, swap Rebuke of the Light’s holy damage to corruption and open with And the Sun Forsook Her Children.

Draw Steel level 3 leader spine (High Elf Ordinator); keeps the Magic keyword. Call the Faithful links Gang Raider (flock members) and Veil Cultist (Concord mentor) statistics. Negotiation: Interest 3, Patience 4; motivations Benevolence and Protection; pitfall Discovery.

CaelMarrow.Name: Ranger-Captain Cael Marrow, “the Gate”
CaelMarrow.Description:
A former Greenline Ranger field-captain who worked this frontier for twenty years, buried too many crews to reclaimed ground that came back wrong, and one day stopped filing reports and stopped going back inside. Verdant lists him as lost on survey; the wastes know him as the reason Cinderhold is still standing. He holds the gate with retired Rangers, Goliar kinship-crews, and anyone who can hold a line.

Stratum: Cinderhold, at the Reach’s outer gate onto the poisoned wastes and the Outer Wall.

Hook: Kestrel Dynamics’ “Clean Route” wants to pave the gate into a logistics depot, and courts Marrow as its credible local face. He knows what Kestrel doesn’t — the corridor runs through ground that is going quiet.

Holds: Cinderhold’s gate and the settlement’s trust: he is its living early-warning system, first to know when a route has gone quiet or the dead-air is spreading.

Answers to / leans on: No one. Leans on old Verdant comrades who slip him seed, water-tech, and ammunition off the books, and a professional back-channel to Mama Cassavir.

Table use: Both: the patron who gives wasteland work and the hard-but-fair authority who can bar a crew from the one safe settlement in the wastes. Ally or wall.

Named Ghostwire level-boss from the Lore Source. Draw Steel level 3 Wode Elf Warleader (leader) math; abilities rethemed to Ghostwire. Placeholder art.
CaelMarrow.Director:
Named boss — echelon 1.

Draw Steel level 3 leader spine (Wode Elf Warleader) rethemed to a ranger longarm (Melee 1 or Ranged 10), ghillie cloak, and smoke; he shifts between shots instead of teleporting. Negotiation: Interest 2, Patience 3; motivations Freedom and Protection; pitfall Greed (Kestrel’s offers). Field retired-Ranger militia as Ironclad or Reach Streets stat blocks reskinned at the table.

Journals.Gazetteer: The Wired — The Flats: Matrix Gazetteer

Vessa.Name: Vessa Corran-Dov — “the Preacher of Ninth”
Vessa.Description: A Corran Street Priest of the Shepherd ministry, holding a lamp-lit corner at Ninth-and-Fold in the Flats. Her Light pact buys mercy and protection, and costs her every time she spends it.

Kaes.Name: Kaïs Vahn-Estal — “the Static Saint”
Kaes.Description: An Elvani Stormcaller who came down off the Glass Tier and stayed down. He runs no chrome — the current he channels will not share a body with metal.

Barak.Name: Barak Voss-Hallor — “the Foreman”
Barak.Description: Nine feet of grey demolition plate and a voice that gets crews paid. The Foreman brokers work in the sprawl and expects the word he gives to be kept.

Wren.Name: Wren Sable-Corvin — “the Kite”
Wren.Description: A Changer of the Raven lineage who works the rooftops and the sightlines above the Flats. She sees the run before the crew walks into it.

Sabbat.Name: Sabbat Vane — “the Dead Frequency”
Sabbat.Description: A Revenant who came back wrong and wired, compiling sprites out of a coffin-motel cell. The dead net answers when he calls, which is not the same as obeying.

Vira.Name: Vira Kellis-Nade — “the Warren-Wire”
Vira.Description: A Changer of the Rat lineage who fights through a fleet she built herself, in warrens she knows nine ways out of. Every drone is a door she left open.

Kessic.Name: Kessic Draye — “Null”
Kessic.Description: An Aberrant-strain Mutant deckhead who turns a site's own defences against the people who paid for them. The taint that marks him is also how he reads a system.

Enabled.Name: Ability sound effects
Enabled.Hint: Play a sound when a hero or NPC uses an ability, fires a weapon, or activates gear.

Volume.Name: Ability SFX volume
Volume.Hint: Volume for Ghostwire ability sounds, on top of Foundry’s own interface volume.

GmOnly.Name: Ability SFX: Director only
GmOnly.Hint: Only Director (GM) clients hear ability sounds.

Sheet.Label: Ghostwire SFX
Sheet.Clear: Clear the override and fall back to the keyword map
Sheet.Hint: Leave empty to use the keyword map (currently matching: {rule}). Foundry core sounds are fine; custom files belong in assets/sfx/.

EquipmentUse.AbilityDescription:
A free strike with your {weapon} ({band} range, {damage} {type} damage on a middle result). Kit bonuses for strikes apply as normal.

This ability is generated from the weapon in your inventory. Remove the weapon and it goes away.

PayloadUse.AbilityDescription:
Fire the {payload} magazine compiled on your deck or Wired Native body-interface.

{effect}

This ability exists while the payload is loaded as a magazine (Load magazine (Craft) on the chip). Each successful run spends one fire; at 0 the magazine is spent and its host slot frees. A loose chip in your gear cannot be run.
PayloadUse.Spent: The {payload} magazine is spent (0 fires). Load a new chip with a Craft (Hacking) Project before you run it.

Zap.Before: Works only on a creature that is Wired (in Overlay or Jacked In). The biofeedback spike hits Stamina directly.

Crash.Tier1: The ICE holds, but you gain an edge on your next roll to breach past it.
Crash.Tier2: The ICE is disabled until the end of your next turn, or you gain a double edge on your next roll to breach past it.
Crash.Tier3: The ICE is disabled for the rest of the encounter.

Whiteout.Target: 1 host within Reach whose Trace Alert you scrub
Whiteout.Before: You must be Connected (Overlay or Jacked In). Spend 1 fire. Target the host whose Trace Alert you are washing, within your deck’s Reach. Foundry v1: the Director adjusts Trace on the Wired Console by hand — this Run does not move the track automatically.
Whiteout.Tier1: The fire is spent. That host’s Trace Alert is unchanged (this overrides the default low +1 Trace).
Whiteout.Tier2: That host’s Trace Alert drops by 1 (minimum 0). Director: click Trace down once on the Wired Console.
Whiteout.Tier3: That host’s Trace Alert drops by 1 (minimum 0), and you cancel the next Trace increase on that host before the end of your next turn (once). Director: click Trace down once, then mark a Whiteout hold on the node notes and skip the next +1 that would land before that deadline.

Ghostload.Before: You plant a trap on this node. It triggers on the next intruder who enters it.
Ghostload.Tier1: The intruder takes biofeedback damage equal to the node's Biofeedback Value.
Ghostload.Tier2: The intruder takes biofeedback damage equal to the node's Biofeedback Value, and their Trace Alert rises by 1.
Ghostload.Tier3: The intruder takes biofeedback damage equal to the node's Biofeedback Value, their Trace Alert rises by 2, and the trap cannot be detected before it fires.

Static.Target: 1 or more enemy devices within Reach
Static.Before: A device is a smartgun link, camera, comm, or hostile drone control. A suppressed device does nothing: no edge, no feed, no signal, no orders.
Static.Tier1: One device is suppressed until the start of your next turn.
Static.Tier2: One device is suppressed until the end of your next turn, and a second device within Reach is suppressed until the start of your next turn.
Static.Tier3: Up to three devices within Reach are suppressed until the end of your next turn.

Blackout.Target: 1 host or small network within Reach
Blackout.Tier1: One host is hard-locked until the end of your next turn.
Blackout.Tier2: A small network crashes until the end of your next turn; its hosts are hard-locked.
Blackout.Tier3: A small network crashes for the rest of the encounter; its hosts are hard-locked.

Wraith.Before: A pre-built master exploit. It is spent on your next host-seizure attempt this encounter (such as Seize Control).
Wraith.Tier1: Your next host-seizure attempt gains an edge.
Wraith.Tier2: Your next host-seizure attempt gains a double edge.
Wraith.Tier3: Your next host-seizure attempt gains a double edge, and the Trace Alert does not rise from it.

PayloadUse.NotLoaded: {payload} isn’t loaded as a magazine. Use Load magazine (Craft) on the chip first.
PayloadUse.NotConnected: {actor} isn’t Connected. Go Overlay or Jacked In before you run {payload}.

Load.Title: Load {payload} magazine
Load.PickDeck: Compile {payload} into a free slot on which host? Cyberdecks and a Technomancer’s Wired Native (body-as-interface) both count. This is a downtime Craft (Hacking) Project: the power roll sets the magazine’s fires (tier 1: 1, tier 2: 3, tier 3: 5).
Load.NoDeck: {payload} needs a cyberdeck or a Wired Native body-interface to compile into; this hero has neither.
Load.NoSlots: {payload} needs a free host slot; every legal host this hero owns is full. Uninstall a suite or a spent magazine first.
Load.NotLoaded: {payload} is no longer loaded as a magazine; nothing to recompile.
Load.Recompiled: {actor} recompiles the {payload} magazine in {deck} ({tier}): now {fires} fire(s).
Load.NoChip: {payload} is spent (quantity 0): there is no chip left to compile. Get a new chip first.

PayloadUse.Dumped: {payload} unloaded: its {fires} remaining fire(s) are dumped. The chip is spent.

GoldLine.Name: Gold Line
GoldLine.Injected: Gold Line is ready under Scenes → Deadhead. Hide the Roofs tile when the crew goes inside.

DeadheadHangout.Name: Deadhead Hangout — Shady Workshop

Voidmark.AvatarHint: Approved L4 plate. Token-ring crop is a later B89 hook.
Voidmark.Empty: The host should not still answer. Ask anyway — Wire procedure, combat budget, chrome, the Accords. The Mark will use the Ghostwire packet it can reach.

Errors.Disabled: VOIDMARK is switched off in Module Configuration.
Errors.Denied: The Director has not opened this channel to runners.
Errors.NoKey: No API key in Module Configuration. The Director pastes it under VOIDMARK settings.

Errors.Empty: The host answered empty. Try again, or check the model id.

Menu.Name: VOIDMARK configuration
Menu.Label: Edit VOIDMARK instructions
Menu.Hint: Opens the persona system-instruction editor plus model / temperature / base URL. The secret API key stays on the main settings list.
Menu.Intro: Persona and Grok-compatible parameters. Paste the API key on the main Ghostwire settings page (password field). Default instructions already speak as VOIDMARK and ground answers in retrieved Ghostwire RAW.

Enabled.Name: Enable VOIDMARK chat
Enabled.Hint: Show the Token-control ghost and allow the VOIDMARK ApplicationV2 to open.

PlayerAccess.Name: VOIDMARK: players may open
PlayerAccess.Hint: Off = GM-only. On = players can chat; the API key stays on the GM client and the ask is relayed by socket.

ApiBaseUrl.Name: VOIDMARK API base URL
ApiBaseUrl.Hint: OpenAI-compatible prefix that owns /chat/completions. xAI: https://api.x.ai/v1

ApiKey.Name: VOIDMARK API key
ApiKey.Hint: Secret world setting. Never pasted into chat or the console. xAI or another OpenAI-compatible provider.

Model.Name: VOIDMARK model
Model.Hint: Chat Completions model id. Default grok-4.6; pick any id your key lists (grok-4.6, grok-4.5, etc.).

Temperature.Name: VOIDMARK temperature
Temperature.Hint: Optional sampling temperature (0–2). Lower stays closer to retrieved RAW.

MaxTokens.Name: VOIDMARK max tokens
MaxTokens.Hint: Optional completion cap sent as max_tokens.

SystemInstructions.Name: VOIDMARK system instructions
SystemInstructions.Hint: Editable persona + boundaries. Retrieved Ghostwire RAW is appended per ask. Leave the default unless you need a table-specific leash.
